subproblem.title: C¹ approximation of Lipschitz maps (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5), vector-valued
subproblem.statement: For all n, p ∈ ℕ, K ≥ 0, every K-Lipschitz map f : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ (ℝᵈ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) and every ε ∈ (0, ∞], there is a map g : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ of class C¹ such that the Lebesgue measure of {x : f(x) ≠ g(x) or Df(x) ≠ Dg(x)} is < ε, where D denotes the Fréchet derivative (Mathlib's fderiv, which is 0 at points of non-differentiability).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n p : ℕ) (f : Rn n → Rn p) (K : ℝ≥0), LipschitzWith K f → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ g : Rn n → Rn p, ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ volume {x | f x ≠ g x ∨ fderiv ℝ f x ≠ fderiv ℝ g x} < ε
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5 (C¹ Approximation Theorem), statement in /mnt/data/zhengyang-workspace/gmt-formalize-claude-opus55-max-20261011/book/chapter-02.txt lines 165-168 (printed p. 42), printed proof lines 246-268 (printed p. 44). It is the result cited in Ch. 3, proof of Lemma 1.2 (chapter-03.txt lines 39-42) and in Ch. 3, (2.4), (2.8), 2.10(2) (chapter-03.txt lines 378-380, 426-428, 440-442). Simon states it for scalar f; the vector-valued statement below follows componentwise (Step 2). Notation: ℝᵏ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), Lⁿ = volume, Dh(x) = fderiv ℝ h x (Mathlib convention: Dh(x) = 0 where h is not differentiable).

Statement. For n, p ∈ ℕ, a K-Lipschitz map f : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ and ε ∈ (0, ∞], there is a C¹ map g : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ with Lⁿ({x : f(x) ≠ g(x) or Df(x) ≠ Dg(x)}) < ε.

Proof.

1. Trivial cases. If ε = ∞ the measure bound only needs finiteness, and the set constructed below has finite measure, so we may assume ε < ∞ (or simply run the construction with ε replaced by 1). If n = 0, then ℝ⁰ = {0}; every map on ℝ⁰ is C¹ (indeed ContDiff), so g := f works and the exceptional set is empty. If p = 0 then ℝᵖ = {0}, f = g = 0 works. Assume n ≥ 1, p ≥ 1, 0 < ε < ∞.

2. Reduction to scalar functions. Write f = Σ_{i=1}^p fⁱ eᵢ with fⁱ := ⟨f, eᵢ⟩ (K-Lipschitz, ℝ-valued). Suppose for each i we have gⁱ ∈ C¹(ℝⁿ, ℝ) with Lⁿ({fⁱ ≠ gⁱ} ∪ {Dfⁱ ≠ Dgⁱ}) < ε/(p+1). Put g := Σ gⁱ eᵢ (C¹). By Rademacher's theorem (Ch. 2, Theorem 1.4, chapter-02.txt lines 62-130; SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.rademacher_ae_differentiableAt) the set Z where f is not differentiable is Lⁿ-null. At x ∉ Z every fⁱ is differentiable with Dfⁱ(x) = ⟨Df(x)(·), eᵢ⟩, so f(x) ≠ g(x) or Df(x) ≠ Dg(x) forces fⁱ(x) ≠ gⁱ(x) or Dfⁱ(x) ≠ Dgⁱ(x) for some i. Hence the exceptional set for f is contained in Z ∪ ⋃ᵢ({fⁱ ≠ gⁱ} ∪ {Dfⁱ ≠ Dgⁱ}), of measure < p·ε/(p+1) < ε. So it suffices to treat f : ℝⁿ → ℝ Lipschitz (Steps 3-8).

3. Differentiability set (Simon line 246). By Rademacher's theorem f is differentiable on a Borel set B with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ B) = 0 (the set of differentiability points of a continuous function is Borel, and x ↦ Df(x) is Borel measurable; Mathlib measurableSet_of_differentiableAt, measurable_fderiv).

4. Lusin (Simon lines 247-249; Ch. 1, Theorem 1.17, chapter-01.txt lines 346-380, SimonGMT IsBorelRegularOuterMeasure.simon_theorem_1_17, “which applies to sets of infinite measure for Lⁿ”). For j ≥ 1 let Aⱼ := {x ∈ B : j − 1 ≤ |x| < j} (Borel, finite measure). Lusin's theorem for real-valued functions (SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable with ν := Lⁿ, its regularity hypothesis supplied by MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt), applied on the finite-measure Borel set Aⱼ to each of the n Borel components x ↦ Df(x)e_l with error ε2^{-j-2}/n, gives closed sets whose intersection Cⱼ ⊆ Aⱼ is closed, satisfies Lⁿ(Aⱼ ∖ Cⱼ) < ε 2^{-j-2}, and Df|Cⱼ is continuous. C := ⋃ⱼ Cⱼ is closed (every bounded set meets only finitely many Cⱼ) and Df|C is continuous (pasting along the locally finite family of closed sets Cⱼ); C ⊆ B and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C) ≤ Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ B) + Σⱼ ε2^{-j-2} < ε/2.

5. Remainder functions (Simon lines 250-257). For x, y ∈ C with y ≠ x put R(x, y) := (f(y) − f(x) − Df(x)(y − x))/|y − x|, and for k ≥ 1, ηₖ(x) := sup{|R(x, y)| : y ∈ C, 0 < |y − x| < 1/k} (sup ∅ := 0) for x ∈ C, ηₖ(x) := 0 for x ∉ C. Since |R(x, y)| ≤ K + ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ 2K (f is K-Lipschitz), ηₖ is real-valued. Since f is differentiable at every x ∈ C ⊆ B, ηₖ(x) ↓ 0 as k → ∞ for every x ∈ C. Each ηₖ is Borel on C: R is continuous on {(x, y) ∈ C × C : x ≠ y} (f continuous, Df|C continuous), so for fixed x the supremum may be taken over y in a fixed countable dense subset D of C (any y ∈ C with 0 < |y − x| < 1/k is a limit of points of D in the same open shell), and ηₖ(x) = sup_{y∈D} 1_{0<|y−x|<1/k}·|R(x, y)| is a countable supremum of Borel functions of x.

6. Egoroff (Simon lines 257-260). For j ≥ 1 apply Egoroff's theorem (Mathlib MeasureTheory.tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto) to the finite measure Lⁿ⌞(C ∩ B_j(0)) and the Borel functions ηₖ → 0: there is a measurable Gⱼ ⊆ C ∩ B_j(0) with Lⁿ((C ∩ B_j(0)) ∖ Gⱼ) < ε 2^{-j-3} on which ηₖ → 0 uniformly. Put A₀ := ⋃ⱼ (Gⱼ ∖ B_{j−1}(0)). Then Lⁿ(C ∖ A₀) < ε/8 and ηₖ → 0 uniformly on A₀ ∩ B_j(0) for each j (A₀ ∩ B_j(0) ⊆ G₁ ∪ … ∪ Gⱼ).

7. Closed set (Simon lines 260-262). For each j choose (inner regularity; MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt) a closed Fⱼ ⊆ Gⱼ ∖ B_{j−1}(0) with Lⁿ((Gⱼ ∖ B_{j−1}(0)) ∖ Fⱼ) < ε2^{-j-3}, and put A := ⋃ⱼ Fⱼ. A is closed because Fⱼ ⊆ {j − 1 ≤ |x| < j}, so the family is locally finite; A ⊆ A₀ and Lⁿ(A₀ ∖ A) < ε/8. Then Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) ≤ Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C) + Lⁿ(C ∖ A₀) + Lⁿ(A₀ ∖ A) < ε/2 + ε/8 + ε/8 < ε.

8. Whitney extension (Simon line 262; Ch. 2, Theorem 1.6, chapter-02.txt lines 173-185; SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney with the structure HasWhitneyC1Compatibility). Take h := f, D := Df on the closed set A. Then h|A and D|A are continuous (Steps 4, A ⊆ C), and for every compact K ⊆ A, sup_{x∈K} ηₖ(x) → 0 (K is bounded, so K ⊆ A₀ ∩ B_j(0) for some j), i.e. for every ε' > 0 there is δ > 0 with |f(y) − f(x) − Df(x)(y − x)| ≤ ε'|y − x| for all x ∈ K, y ∈ A, |x − y| < δ: this is exactly the hypothesis 1.6(‡) (the remainder field of HasWhitneyC1Compatibility). Whitney's theorem gives g ∈ C¹(ℝⁿ) with g = f on A and Dg(a) = Df(a) for every a ∈ A (HasFDerivAt g (Df a) a). Hence {f ≠ g} ∪ {Df ≠ Dg} ⊆ ℝⁿ ∖ A, which has measure < ε by Step 7. ∎

Remark (no departure from the book except the explicit vector-valued reduction in Step 2 and the bookkeeping of Lusin/Egoroff on the σ-finite measure Lⁿ, which Simon indicates in lines 247-260).
proof_key_steps: Dispose of n = 0, p = 0 and ε = ∞; reduce to scalar f componentwise using Rademacher's theorem.
Rademacher: f is differentiable on a Borel set of full measure, with Borel derivative.
Lusin on annuli: a closed C of co-measure < ε/2 on which Df is continuous.
Remainders ηₖ(x) = sup_{y∈C, 0<|y−x|<1/k}|R(x,y)| are Borel and decrease to 0 on C.
Egoroff on bounded pieces and inner regularity: a closed A of co-measure < ε on which ηₖ → 0 uniformly on compacts (Whitney's hypothesis 1.6(‡)).
Whitney extension (SimonGMT exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney): C¹ g with g = f and Dg = Df on A.

subproblem.title: Approximate tangent planes and tangential differentials along C¹ charts (Simon Remarks 1.5(2), 1.8(1); Ch. 2 (4.8)-(4.10))
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ, p ∈ ℕ, N = n + ℓ. Let M ⊆ ℝ^N be Hⁿ-measurable, θ a positive locally integrable weight on M (θ > 0 on M, θ is Hⁿ⌞M-measurable, ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K), U ⊇ M open, f : ℝ^N → ℝᵖ locally Lipschitz on U, V ⊆ ℝⁿ open and ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N of class C¹ on V with injective derivative Dψ(u) at every u ∈ V. Then for Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ V with ψ(u) ∈ M: (A) M has approximate tangent space range Dψ(u) at ψ(u) with respect to θ in the sense of Simon's Definition 1.7 (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt); (B) f ∘ ψ is differentiable at u; (C) for every w ∈ ℝⁿ, t ↦ f(ψ(u) + t·Dψ(u)w) has derivative D(f∘ψ)(u)w at t = 0 (HasLineDerivAt).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ p : ℕ) (M U : Set (Rn (n + ℓ))) (θ : Rn (n + ℓ) → ℝ) (f : Rn (n + ℓ) → Rn p) (V : Set (Rn n)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn (n + ℓ)), NullMeasurableSet M μHE[n] → IsPositiveLocallyIntegrableWeight n M θ → IsOpen U → M ⊆ U → LocallyLipschitzOn U f → IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → (∀ u ∈ V, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ u)) → ∀ᵐ u ∂(volume : Measure (Rn n)), u ∈ V → ψ u ∈ M → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ (ψ u) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ ψ u).toLinearMap) ∧ DifferentiableAt ℝ (f ∘ ψ) u ∧ ∀ w : Rn n, HasLineDerivAt ℝ f (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ ψ) u w) (ψ u) (fderiv ℝ ψ u w)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Part (A) is Simon's Remark 1.5(2) (chapter-03.txt lines 87-90), proved in the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒” (lines 113-143), in the weighted form of Remark 1.8(1) (lines 298-306, multiplicity θ of Definition 1.7, lines 284-295), localized to one C¹ chart. Parts (B), (C) are Simon Ch. 2, (4.8)-(4.10) (chapter-02.txt lines ≈ 925-957, printed pp. 56-57): Rademacher's theorem in local coordinates and the identification of the tangential directional derivative with the ambient one for f locally Lipschitz on an open set. The book uses these facts in Ch. 3 §2 (lines 343-350: “T_yM agrees with T_yN_j for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M_j” and “D_τf(y) = d/dt f(y + tτ)|_{t=0}”). Detail added: the book argues for embedded submanifolds; we argue on small balls of a C¹ immersion, which is all that is needed (injectivity of ψ on V is not used).

Notation. N = n + ℓ; ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d); Hⁿ = μHE[n]; Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ (= Hⁿ there); B_ρ(x) open ball, B̄ closed ball; ω_n = Lⁿ(B_1(0)); η_{x,λ}(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x); Jψ(u) := normDet(Dψ(u)) = √det(Dψ(u)*Dψ(u)). For x ∈ ℝ^N, λ > 0 and A ⊆ ℝ^N: (F1) ∫_{η_{x,λ}(A)} g dHⁿ = λ^{-n}∫_A g∘η_{x,λ} dHⁿ for every Borel g ≥ 0 and for every g with g∘η_{x,λ} ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞A) (equivalently g ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞η_{x,λ}(A))), because η_{x,λ} is a similarity of ratio λ⁻¹, so Hⁿ(η_{x,λ}(S)) = λ^{-n}Hⁿ(S) for every S (scaling and translation invariance of Hausdorff measure), i.e. (η_{x,λ})_#(Hⁿ⌞A) = λⁿ Hⁿ⌞η_{x,λ}(A). (F2) A K-Lipschitz map does not increase Hⁿ by more than the factor Kⁿ (SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn), so locally Lipschitz maps on open sets send Hⁿ-null sets to Hⁿ-null sets.

Statement. (Hypotheses as in the Lean statement.) For Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ V with ψ(u) ∈ M: (A) HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ (ψ u) (range Dψ(u)); (B) f∘ψ is differentiable at u; (C) ∀ w ∈ ℝⁿ, HasLineDerivAt ℝ f (D(f∘ψ)(u) w) (ψ u) (Dψ(u) w).

Proof.

1. Case n = 0. Then ℝ⁰ = {0} and, if V ≠ ∅, u = 0, Dψ(0) is the zero map on the zero space (injective) with range {0} (finrank 0). H⁰ is counting measure and ∫_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ = Σ_{z∈M∩K} θ(z) < ∞ for compact K. For x = ψ(0) ∈ M and f₀ ∈ C_c with spt f₀ ⊆ B_R(0): ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)} f₀(y)θ(x + λy) dH⁰(y) = Σ_{z∈M} f₀((z − x)/λ) θ(z); for λ ≤ 1 only z ∈ M ∩ B̄_R(x) contribute, the terms are dominated by ‖f₀‖_∞θ(z) (summable), and each term with z ≠ x tends to 0 (|z − x|/λ → ∞), so the sum tends to f₀(0)θ(x) = θ(x)∫_{{0}} f₀ dH⁰. Hence (A) holds. (B) holds since every map on the 0-dimensional space is differentiable, and (C) holds because the only direction is w = 0 and t ↦ f(x + t·0) is constant (derivative 0 = D(f∘ψ)(0)0). Assume n ≥ 1.

2. Localization. For u₀ ∈ V let c₀ := min_{|v|=1}|Dψ(u₀)v| > 0 and choose r₀ = r(u₀) > 0 with B̄_{2r₀}(u₀) ⊆ V and ‖Dψ(u) − Dψ(u₀)‖ ≤ c₀/2 on B̄_{2r₀}(u₀) (continuity of Dψ on the open V, ψ being C¹ there). By the mean value inequality on the convex ball, for u, u' ∈ B̄_{2r₀}(u₀): |ψ(u) − ψ(u') − Dψ(u₀)(u − u')| ≤ (c₀/2)|u − u'|, hence (c₀/2)|u − u'| ≤ |ψ(u) − ψ(u')| ≤ Λ|u − u'| with Λ := ‖Dψ(u₀)‖ + c₀/2. So ψ is injective and bi-Lipschitz on B̄_{2r₀}(u₀). V is covered by countably many balls B_{r(uᵢ)}(uᵢ) (Lindelöf), so it suffices to prove (A)-(C) for Lⁿ-a.e. u in one ball B := B_{r₀}(u₀). Put Σ := ψ(B).
 Facts. (Σ1) ψ|B̄_{2r₀}(u₀) is a homeomorphism onto the compact set ψ(B̄_{2r₀}(u₀)), so Σ is relatively open in a compact set, hence Borel. (Σ2) Injective area formula (Simon Ch. 2, (3.2), (4.13); SimonGMT injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn and weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum for the injective Lipschitz map ψ on the open B, where the Jacobian within B is Jψ): ∫_Σ h dHⁿ = ∫_B h(ψ(u)) Jψ(u) du for every Borel h ≥ 0, and hence for bounded Borel h with bounded support (apply it to h⁺ and h⁻; both sides finite); in particular Hⁿ(Σ) < ∞, and for x = ψ(u) ∈ Σ, ρ > 0: Hⁿ(Σ ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ C₁ρⁿ with C₁ := ω_n (2Λ/c₀)ⁿ (because B ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄_ρ(x)) ⊆ B̄_{2ρ/c₀}(u) and Jψ ≤ Λⁿ), and Hⁿ(Σ ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) > 0 (because B ∩ B_{ρ/Λ}(u) ⊆ ψ⁻¹(B̄_ρ(x)) and Jψ ≥ (c₀/2)ⁿ). (Σ3) For Z ⊆ B: Lⁿ(Z) = 0 iff Hⁿ(ψ(Z)) = 0 (F2 for ψ and for ψ⁻¹ on Σ).

3. Three density properties. Let S := M ∩ Σ (Hⁿ-measurable). Let ν₁ := θHⁿ⌞(M ∖ Σ), i.e. ν₁(A') := ∫_{A' ∩ (M∖Σ)} θ dHⁿ (a Borel regular measure, finite on compact sets by the hypothesis on θ), and ν₂ := Hⁿ⌞(Σ ∖ M) (finite).
 (P1) For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S: ρ^{-n}∫_{(M∖Σ)∩B_ρ(x)} θ dHⁿ → 0. This is the Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6 and Remark 3.7(2), chapter-01.txt lines 700-715; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6, simon_remark_3_7_of_openSigmaFinite) applied to the open-σ-finite Borel regular measure ν₁ and the ν₁-measurable set M ∖ Σ: Θ^{*n}(ν₁, M ∖ Σ, x) = 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ M ∖ Σ, in particular for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S (open balls are contained in closed ones).
 (P2) For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S: ρ^{-n}Hⁿ((Σ ∖ M) ∩ B_ρ(x)) → 0. Same theorem for the finite measure Hⁿ⌞Σ and the set Σ ∖ M (x ∈ S ⇒ x ∉ Σ ∖ M).

subproblem.title: Eilenberg's inequality for slices of Lipschitz maps (Simon Ch. 2, Theorems 1.8(ii)-1.9, upper-integral form)
subproblem.statement: For all N, m, k ∈ ℕ there is a constant C ≥ 0 such that for every set A ⊆ ℝ^N (not necessarily measurable), every L ≥ 0 and every L-Lipschitz map f : ℝ^N → ℝᵐ there is a Borel measurable g : ℝᵐ → [0, ∞] with Hᵏ(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ g(y) for every y ∈ ℝᵐ and ∫ g dLᵐ ≤ C·L^m·H^{m+k}(A), where Hᵈ = μHE[d] is the Euclidean-normalized d-dimensional Hausdorff (outer) measure on ℝ^N and Lᵐ = volume on ℝᵐ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N m k : ℕ), ∃ C : ℝ≥0, ∀ (A : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m) (L : ℝ≥0), LipschitzWith L f → ∃ g : Rn m → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g ∧ (∀ y, μHE[k] (A ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}) ≤ g y) ∧ ∫⁻ y, g y ≤ ((C * L ^ m : ℝ≥0) : ℝ≥0∞) * μHE[m + k] A
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 2, Theorem 1.8(ii) (k = 0 case) and Theorem 1.9 with Remark 1.10 (upper Lebesgue integral), chapter-02.txt lines 270-333 (1.8) and 335-400 (1.9, its proof lines 366-400), printed pp. 44-46. Simon proves exactly the upper-integral inequality below (lines 366-397); his additional measurability assertion is not needed here and is not claimed. Constants: we do not use the isodiametric inequality (Simon's sharp constant ω_mω_k/ω_{m+k}); any constant C(m, k) suffices.

Notation. ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d); for s ≥ 0, Hˢ = μHE[s] on ℝ^N. Mathlib's μHE[s] equals c_s·μH[s], where μH[s] = sup_{δ>0} μH[s]_δ is the Hausdorff measure built from covers by sets of diameter ≤ δ with cost diam^s (cost 1 for every nonempty set when s = 0; H⁰ is counting measure). Write H^s_δ(S) := inf{Σᵢ c_s (diam Cᵢ)^s : S ⊆ ⋃ᵢ Cᵢ, diam Cᵢ ≤ δ}, so H^s_δ ↑ Hˢ as δ ↓ 0 and covers may be taken by closed sets (diam C̄ = diam C). λₘ = volume (Lebesgue measure) on ℝᵐ; ωₘ := λₘ(B_1(0)) (ω₀ = 1). The Lipschitz constant is L and Lᵐ below always means its m-th power.

Statement. For N, m, k ∈ ℕ there is C ≥ 0 such that for all A ⊆ ℝ^N, L ≥ 0 and L-Lipschitz f : ℝ^N → ℝᵐ there is a Borel g : ℝᵐ → [0, ∞] with Hᵏ(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ g(y) for all y and ∫ g dλₘ ≤ C·Lᵐ·H^{m+k}(A).

Proof. Put C := ωₘ·c_k / c_{m+k} (positive; for m = 0 this is 1).

1. Elementary volume bound. For S ⊆ ℝᵐ nonempty, S ⊆ B̄_{diam S}(s₀) for any s₀ ∈ S, hence λₘ(S̄) ≤ ωₘ (diam S)ᵐ (for m = 0, λ₀ is the unit point mass and the bound reads 1 ≤ 1). If f is L-Lipschitz and C ⊆ ℝ^N then diam f(C) ≤ L diam C, so λₘ(closure f(C)) ≤ ωₘ Lᵐ (diam C)ᵐ.

2. Case L = 0. Then f ≡ y₀ is constant and A ∩ f⁻¹{y} is A for y = y₀ and ∅ otherwise. Take g := Hᵏ(A)·1_{{y₀}} (Borel). If m ≥ 1 then ∫ g dλₘ = Hᵏ(A)·λₘ({y₀}) = 0 (with ∞·0 = 0). If m = 0 then ∫ g = Hᵏ(A) = C·L⁰·H^{0+k}(A) (C = 1, L⁰ = 1). Assume L > 0.

3. Case H^{m+k}(A) = ∞. Take g :≡ ∞; then ∫ g ≤ ∞ = C·Lᵐ·H^{m+k}(A) since C > 0, L > 0. Assume H^{m+k}(A) < ∞.

4. Covers (Simon (1), lines 366-369). For each i ≥ 1 choose closed sets C_{i1}, C_{i2}, … with A ⊆ ⋃ⱼ C_{ij}, diam C_{ij} ≤ 1/i, and Σⱼ c_{m+k}(diam C_{ij})^{m+k} ≤ H^{m+k}_{1/i}(A) + 1/i (discard empty sets). Define the Borel simple-type functions (Simon lines 369-372)
 gᵢ(y) := Σⱼ c_k (diam C_{ij})^k · 1_{K_{ij}}(y), K_{ij} := closure of f(C_{ij}) (closed, hence Borel).
 (For k = 0 the coefficient is c₀·1.)

5. Pointwise bound (Simon (2), lines 373-377). Fix y. A ∩ f⁻¹{y} ⊆ ⋃_{j : y ∈ f(C_{ij})} C_{ij}, a cover by sets of diameter ≤ 1/i, so H^k_{1/i}(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ Σ_{j : y ∈ f(C_{ij})} c_k (diam C_{ij})^k ≤ gᵢ(y).

6. Integral bound (Simon lines 377-385). By monotone convergence and Step 1,
 ∫ gᵢ dλₘ = Σⱼ c_k (diam C_{ij})^k λₘ(K_{ij}) ≤ Σⱼ c_k ωₘ Lᵐ (diam C_{ij})^{m+k} = C Lᵐ Σⱼ c_{m+k}(diam C_{ij})^{m+k} ≤ C Lᵐ (H^{m+k}_{1/i}(A) + 1/i).

7. Limit (Simon lines 385-393; Remark 1.10). Let g := liminf_{i→∞} gᵢ (Borel). For every y, Hᵏ(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = lim_i H^k_{1/i}(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ liminf_i gᵢ(y) = g(y) by Step 5. By Fatou's lemma and Step 6, ∫ g dλₘ ≤ liminf_i ∫ gᵢ ≤ liminf_i C Lᵐ (H^{m+k}_{1/i}(A) + 1/i) ≤ C Lᵐ H^{m+k}(A), because H^{m+k}_{1/i}(A) ≤ H^{m+k}(A). ∎

Remarks. (i) No measurability of A is used (Simon's proof of the inequality uses only covers; his measurability hypothesis serves the separate measurability assertion, which is not part of this statement). (ii) Consequences used by siblings: if H^{m+k}(A) = 0 then Hᵏ(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = 0 for λₘ-a.e. y (g = 0 a.e.); if H^{m+k}(A) < ∞ then Hᵏ(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) < ∞ for λₘ-a.e. y (g < ∞ a.e.).

For each i cover A by closed sets C_{ij} of diameter ≤ 1/i nearly realizing H^{m+k}_{1/i}(A).
Define Borel gᵢ := Σⱼ c_k(diam C_{ij})^k 1_{closure f(C_{ij})}; then H^k_{1/i}(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ gᵢ(y).
Bound ∫gᵢ using Lᵐ(closure f(C)) ≤ ωₘ(L diam C)ᵐ.
g := liminf gᵢ; Fatou gives ∫g ≤ C L^m H^{m+k}(A), and Hᵏ = lim H^k_{1/i} gives the pointwise bound.

subproblem.title: (4.1): Gauss-Green representation of sets of locally finite perimeter, with uniqueness
subproblem.statement: For n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} open and E ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} Lebesgue null-measurable: (i) E has locally finite perimeter in U (χ_E ∈ BV_loc(U) in the sense of SimonGMT IsLocallyBV) iff there are a Borel measure μ on ℝ^{n+1} and ν : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+1} forming a Gauss-Green pair (μ(ℝ^{n+1} ∖ U) = 0, μ finite on compact subsets of U, ν μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ν| = 1 μ-a.e., and ∫_{E∩U} div g = −∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ for every C¹ compactly supported g with tsupport g ⊆ U); (ii) any two Gauss-Green pairs (μ, ν), (μ', ν') for (U, E) satisfy μ = μ' and ν = ν' μ-a.e.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 3, §4, the paragraph defining sets of locally finite perimeter and (4.1), chapter-03.txt lines 555-573 (printed p. 80): “E has locally finite perimeter in U if χ_E is in BV_loc(U) (See §2 of Ch. 2.) Thus E has locally finite perimeter in U if there is a Radon measure μ_E (= |Dχ_E| in the notation of §2 of Ch. 2) on U and a μ_E-measurable ν with |ν| = 1 μ_E-a.e. in U such that (4.1) ∫_{E∩U} div g dL^{n+1} = −∫_U g·ν dμ_E”. The printed justification is Simon Ch. 2, §2, (2.1)-(2.4) (chapter-02.txt lines 477-530, printed pp. 48-49): the functional ∫ u div g extends to compactly supported continuous fields and the Riesz representation theorem (Ch. 1, 4.14) gives μ, ν; “|Du| … is uniquely characterized by (2.4)”. We fill in the extension step, the converse, and the uniqueness (which the book asserts through the phrase “the” measure |Dχ_E|). Sign: the contract (and the printed (4.1)) has the minus sign, so ν is the inward normal; Ch. 2 (2.2) is printed without it, which only changes ν to −ν.

Notation. N := n + 1, ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), L^N = volume, div g = trace of Dg (SimonGMT euclideanDivergence). A Gauss-Green pair (μ, ν) for (U, E) (IsGaussGreenPair) means: μ a Borel measure on ℝ^N with μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0 and μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; ν μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ν| = 1 μ-a.e.; and (GG) ∫_{E∩U} div g dL^N = −∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ for every C¹ g : ℝ^N → ℝ^N with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ U. HasLocallyFinitePerimeter U E is SimonGMT IsLocallyBV U χ_E: U open, χ_E locally integrable on U, and for every open W with W̄ compact ⊆ U there is c(W) ≥ 0 with ∫_W χ_E div g ≤ c(W)·sup|g| for all C¹ g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ^N) with tsupport g ⊆ W.

Statement. For U open and E Lebesgue-null-measurable: (i) HasLocallyFinitePerimeter U E ⟺ ∃ μ ν, IsGaussGreenPair U E μ ν; (ii) any two pairs (μ, ν), (μ', ν') satisfy μ = μ' and ν = ν' μ-a.e.

Proof.

1. Two remarks. (R1) If g is C¹ with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ W ⊆ U then div g = 0 off tsupport g (SimonGMT support_euclideanDivergence_subset), so ∫_{E∩U} div g = ∫_{E∩W} div g = ∫_W χ_E div g. (R2) For g as in (GG), x ↦ ⟨g(x), ν(x)⟩ is bounded and vanishes off the compact tsupport g ⊆ U, where μ is finite; so it is μ-integrable and |∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ| ≤ sup|g|·μ(tsupport g).

2. “⇐”. Let (μ, ν) be a pair. U is open by hypothesis. χ_E is measurable for the completed Lebesgue measure (E is null-measurable) and bounded, hence locally integrable on U. Let W be open with W̄ compact ⊆ U and put c(W) := μ(W̄) (finite, ≥ 0). For C¹ g ∈ C_c with tsupport g ⊆ W: by (R1), (GG), |ν| = 1 a.e. and (R2), ∫_W χ_E div g = ∫_{E∩U} div g = −∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ ≤ ∫_{tsupport g}|g| dμ ≤ sup|g|·μ(W̄). Since compactlySupportedSupNorm g = sup_x |g(x)|, IsLocallyBV U χ_E holds.

3. “⇒”, Step 1: the functional on C¹ fields (Simon Ch. 2, (2.1), lines 482-493). Assume IsLocallyBV U χ_E. For C¹ g with compact support in U set Λ(g) := ∫_{E∩U} div g. If tsupport g ⊆ W (W open, W̄ compact ⊆ U), then by (R1) Λ(g) = ∫_W χ_E div g ≤ c(W) sup|g|, and applying this to −g, |Λ(g)| ≤ c(W) sup|g|.

4. “⇒”, Step 2: extension to continuous fields (Simon lines 485-490: “the functional ∫ u div g extends uniquely to give a linear functional on K(U, ℝⁿ) … bounded on K_W(U, ℝⁿ) for every W ⊂⊂ U”). Let g : ℝ^N → ℝ^N be continuous with compact support K ⊆ U. Choose an open W with K ⊆ W, W̄ compact ⊆ U, and σ₀ < dist(K, ℝ^N ∖ W). The mollifications g_σ := φ_σ * g (σ < σ₀, φ_σ a standard mollifier) are C^∞ with support in the σ-neighbourhood of K ⊆ W and g_σ → g uniformly as σ → 0. By Step 3, |Λ(g_σ) − Λ(g_τ)| ≤ c(W) sup|g_σ − g_τ| → 0, so Λ̃(g) := lim_{σ→0} Λ(g_σ) exists. The limit does not depend on choices: for any sequence of C¹ fields hᵢ → g uniformly with supports in a fixed compact subset of U, |Λ(hᵢ) − Λ(g_σ)| ≤ c(W') sup|hᵢ − g_σ| for a W' ⊂⊂ U containing all supports. Hence Λ̃ is linear on the space of compactly supported continuous fields with support in U, extends Λ (take hᵢ = g for g ∈ C¹), and |Λ̃(g)| ≤ c(W) sup|g| whenever spt g is a compact subset of the open W ⊂⊂ U. In particular Λ̃ is a locally bounded linear functional on C_c(U, ℝ^N) (U with the subspace topology is locally compact Hausdorff; continuous fields with compact support in U correspond to elements of C_c(U, ℝ^N) by restriction and extension by 0).

5. “⇒”, Step 3: Riesz representation (Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 4.14, chapter-01.txt line 1654; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_4_14 for the locally compact Hausdorff space X := U and H := ℝ^N). There are a Radon measure μ_U on U and a μ_U-measurable ν_U : U → ℝ^N with |ν_U| = 1 μ_U-a.e. and Λ̃(g) = ∫_U ⟨g, ν_U⟩ dμ_U for all g ∈ C_c(U, ℝ^N). Let μ be the Borel measure on ℝ^N given by μ(B) := μ_U(B ∩ U) (push-forward under the inclusion; Borel sets of U are traces of Borel sets of ℝ^N because U is open), and ν := −ν_U on U, ν := e₁ off U. Here simon_theorem_4_14 provides a Radon outer measure with ν_U measurable for its Carathéodory σ-algebra; since μ_U is Borel regular on the σ-compact space U, every μ_U-measurable set differs from a Borel set by a μ_U-null set, so ν_U = ν̃_U μ_U-a.e. for a Borel ν̃_U, and integrals of Borel integrands against the Carathéodory measure equal those against its restriction to Borel sets; use ν̃_U in place of ν_U. Then μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) = μ_U(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (Radon), ν is Borel, hence μ-a.e. strongly measurable, with |ν| = 1 μ-a.e., and for C¹ g with compact support in U: ∫_{E∩U} div g = Λ(g) = Λ̃(g) = ∫⟨g, ν_U⟩dμ = −∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ. So (μ, ν) is a Gauss-Green pair.

6. Uniqueness, Step 1. Let (μ, ν), (μ', ν') be pairs. By (GG), ∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ = ∫⟨g, ν'⟩dμ' for all C¹ g with compact support in U; by mollification (uniform convergence with supports in a fixed compact subset of U, where μ, μ' are finite, and dominated convergence) the identity extends to all continuous g with compact support in U.

7. Uniqueness, Step 2: total variation on open sets (Simon Ch. 2, (2.4), lines 518-526: |Du| “is uniquely characterized by” its values on open W ⊂⊂ U). For open O ⊆ U: μ(O) = sup{∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ : g continuous, spt g compact ⊆ O, |g| ≤ 1}. “≥” follows from (R2)-type estimate ∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ ≤ ∫_O |g| dμ ≤ μ(O). “≤”: let K ⊆ O be compact and ε > 0. Choose a compact L ⊆ O with K ⊆ int L and μ(L ∖ K) < ε (the closed η-neighbourhoods L_η of K decrease to K, μ(L_η) < ∞ for small η). By Lusin's theorem (SimonGMT IsBorelRegularOuterMeasure.simon_theorem_1_17 or Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable for the finite measure μ⌞L, applied to the N real coordinates of ν with error ε/(2N) each, and intersecting the resulting closed sets; also discard the null set where |ν| ≠ 1) there is a compact K' ⊆ K with μ(K ∖ K') < ε on which ν is continuous with |ν| = 1. Extend ν|K' to a continuous map ℝ^N → ℝ^N (Tietze, coordinatewise), compose with the radial retraction r(z) := z/max(1, |z|) onto the closed unit ball, and multiply by a continuous cut-off χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on K, spt χ ⊆ L. The resulting g is admissible and ∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ ≥ μ(K') − μ(L ∖ K') ≥ μ(K) − ε − (μ(L ∖ K) + ε) ≥ μ(K) − 3ε. Since μ(O) = sup{μ(K) : K ⊆ O compact} (inner regularity of the locally finite Borel measure μ⌞U on the open set U), “≤” follows. The same holds for (μ', ν'), and by Step 6 the two suprema coincide: μ(O) = μ'(O) for every open O ⊆ U.

8. Uniqueness, Step 3: μ = μ'. Both measures vanish on ℝ^N ∖ U and are locally finite Borel measures on the σ-compact open set U, hence outer regular there; agreeing on open subsets of U, they agree on all Borel subsets of U, and μ(B) = μ(B ∩ U) = μ'(B ∩ U) = μ'(B) for every Borel B. So μ = μ'.

9. Uniqueness, Step 4: ν = ν' μ-a.e. With μ = μ', ∫⟨g, ν − ν'⟩dμ = 0 for all continuous g with compact support in U (Step 6). Fix a compact K ⊆ U. Continuous compactly supported fields are dense in L¹(μ⌞L; ℝ^N) for a compact neighbourhood L ⊆ U of K; choose such gᵢ → (ν − ν')1_K in L¹(μ) with |gᵢ| ≤ 2 (truncate by the radial retraction onto the ball of radius 2). Since ν − ν' is bounded, ∫_K |ν − ν'|² dμ = lim ∫⟨gᵢ, ν − ν'⟩dμ = 0, so ν = ν' μ-a.e. on K. U is a countable union of compact sets and μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0, so ν = ν' μ-a.e. ∎
proof_key_steps: '⇐': the pair identity bounds ∫_W χ_E div g by μ(W̄)·sup|g|.
'⇒': the BV bound makes g ↦ ∫_{E∩U} div g locally bounded on C¹ fields; extend by mollification to compactly supported continuous fields.
Riesz representation (Simon Ch. 1, 4.14; SimonGMT simon_theorem_4_14) on U gives μ_U, ν_U; push μ_U to ℝ^{n+1} and set ν := −ν_U (Borel version).
Uniqueness: the pairings ∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ agree for all continuous compactly supported g.
μ(O) = sup{∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ : |g| ≤ 1, spt g ⊆ O} (Lusin + Tietze), so μ and μ' agree on open subsets of U, hence everywhere (outer regularity).
ν = ν' μ-a.e. by density of continuous fields in L¹(μ⌞K).

subproblem.title: A measure with approximate tangent planes of positive multiplicity a.e. is carried by a countably n-rectifiable Borel set (Simon 1.6 '⇐', measure form)
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, N = n + ℓ, and let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^N with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K. Assume that for μ-a.e. x there are a subspace P and θ > 0 such that HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x P θ holds, i.e. finrank P = n and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), (rⁿ)⁻¹∫ f(η_{x,r}(y)) dμ(y) → θ∫_P f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0, where η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x). Then there is a Borel set R ⊆ ℝ^N which is countably n-rectifiable and satisfies μ(ℝ^N ∖ R) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Rn (n + ℓ))), (∀ K : Set (Rn (n + ℓ)), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∃ (P : Submodule ℝ (Rn (n + ℓ))) (θ : ℝ), 0 < θ ∧ HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x P θ) → ∃ R : Set (Rn (n + ℓ)), MeasurableSet R ∧ CountablyRectifiable n R ∧ μ Rᶜ = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. This is the argument of Simon's proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇐” (chapter-03.txt lines 145-274, printed pp. 72-74) together with Remark 1.5(3) (lines 91-105), written for a general locally finite Borel measure μ with approximate tangent planes of positive (variable) multiplicity instead of μ = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ B_R(0)) with multiplicity 1. Simon's proof only uses the density property (5) and the cone property (6) of μ at points of a set of full measure, so it applies verbatim to such μ; the book itself uses it in this generality for μ_E in the proof of 4.3 (“By 1.6 …”, line 604). Departures from the printed text, stated explicitly: (a) the printed choice ε = 1/16ⁿ in (9)-(10) is too large: (9) only gives μ(B_{ρ/8}(y)) ≥ (1−ε)ω_n(ρ/8)ⁿ, not ≥ ω_n(ρ/8)ⁿ as printed on line 246, and then the contradiction needs ε < 1/(1+16ⁿ); (b) Simon applies Egoroff to qₖ(x), defined with the x-dependent normal plane π_x, without addressing measurability of x ↦ π_x; we instead use finitely many fixed planes (whence slightly different cone constants: 1/3 and B_{ρ/16}); (c) multiplicities θ_x ∈ (0, ∞) are handled by sorting points into dyadic density classes; (d) the iteration (lines 263-274) is done by shrinking the target set instead of restricting μ.

Notation. N = n + ℓ, ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), B_ρ(x) open ball, ω_n = Lⁿ(B_1(0)), η_{x,λ}(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x). For an n-dimensional subspace P, q_P is the orthogonal projection onto P and Hⁿ⌞P is Lebesgue measure on P, so Hⁿ(P ∩ B_r(0)) = ω_n rⁿ. Hypothesis (H): for μ-a.e. x there are P_x (finrank n) and θ_x > 0 with λ^{-n}∫ f(η_{x,λ}(y)) dμ(y) → θ_x ∫_{P_x} f dHⁿ (λ ↓ 0) for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ). Goal: a Borel, countably n-rectifiable R with μ(ℝ^N ∖ R) = 0.

Proof.

1. Reduction to finite μ. Suppose the result holds for finite measures. For k ∈ ℕ let μₖ := μ⌞B_k(0) (finite since B̄_k(0) is compact). If x ∈ B_k(0) satisfies (H) for μ, it satisfies (H) for μₖ with the same (P_x, θ_x): for f ∈ C_c with spt f ⊆ B_R(0) and λ < (k − |x|)/R, f(η_{x,λ}(y)) ≠ 0 forces y ∈ B_{λR}(x) ⊆ B_k(0), so the integrals for μ and μₖ coincide. Points outside B_k(0) form a μₖ-null set, and the μ-null exceptional set is μₖ-null. So (H) holds for μₖ; let Rₖ be the corresponding Borel rectifiable set and R := ⋃ₖ Rₖ (Borel; countably n-rectifiable as a countable union, SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion). Then μ(ℝ^N ∖ R) ≤ Σₖ μ(B_k(0) ∖ Rₖ) = Σₖ μₖ(ℝ^N ∖ Rₖ) = 0. Henceforth μ(ℝ^N) < ∞.

2. Trivial dimensions. If ℓ = 0, R := ℝ^N = range(id) works. If n = 0, then finrank P_x = 0 forces P_x = ⊥ = {0} (Submodule.finrank_eq_zero), μHE[0] = μH[0] is counting measure (μH[0]{x} = 1, Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton), (r⁰)⁻¹ = 1, and ∫_{{0}} f dH⁰ = f(0). Taking f ∈ C_c with 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, f(0) = 1, spt f ⊆ B_1(0): ∫ f∘η_{x,λ} dμ ≤ μ(B_λ(x)) ↓ μ({x}) and the left side → θ_x f(0) = θ_x, so μ({x}) ≥ θ_x > 0 for μ-a.e. x. The atom set R := {x : μ({x}) > 0} is countable (μ finite), hence Borel and countably 0-rectifiable (a countable union of ranges of constant maps ℝ⁰ → ℝ^N), and μ(ℝ^N ∖ R) = 0. Assume from now on n ≥ 1 and ℓ ≥ 1.

3. Pointwise consequences of (H) (Simon Remark 1.5(3), lines 91-105, with multiplicity). Let x satisfy (H), P := P_x, θ := θ_x, and for α ∈ (0, 1) let K_α(P) := {z : |q_P z| ≤ α|z|} (closed cone around P^⊥, i.e. Simon's X_α(π_x, 0) with π_x = P^⊥, lines 151-157).
 (5') lim_{ρ↓0} μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρⁿ) = θ. Indeed, for 0 < τ < 1 pick f, g ∈ C_c with 0 ≤ f, g ≤ 1, f = 1 on B̄_1(0), spt f ⊆ B_{1+τ}(0), g = 1 on B̄_{1−τ}(0), spt g ⊆ B_1(0). Then ∫ g∘η_{x,ρ} dμ ≤ μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ ∫ f∘η_{x,ρ} dμ; dividing by ρⁿ and letting ρ ↓ 0 gives θ ω_n (1−τ)ⁿ ≤ θ∫_P g ≤ liminf ≤ limsup ≤ θ∫_P f ≤ θ ω_n (1+τ)ⁿ; let τ ↓ 0.
 (6') lim_{ρ↓0} ρ^{-n} μ((x + K_{1/2}(P)) ∩ B_ρ(x)) = 0. Indeed (x + K_{1/2}(P)) ∩ B_ρ(x) = x + ρ S₀ with S₀ := K_{1/2}(P) ∩ B_1(0) ⊆ S := K_{1/2}(P) ∩ B̄_1(0) (compact). With f_j(z) := max(0, 1 − j·dist(z, S)) ∈ C_c, f_j ≥ 1_S: ρ^{-n}μ(x + ρS₀) ≤ ρ^{-n}∫ f_j∘η_{x,ρ} dμ → θ∫_P f_j dHⁿ, and ∫_P f_j dHⁿ ↓ Hⁿ(P ∩ S) = Hⁿ({0}) = 0 as j → ∞ (dominated convergence on the bounded set P ∩ B̄_2(0); P ∩ K_{1/2}(P) = {z ∈ P : |z| ≤ |z|/2} = {0}; n ≥ 1).

4. Fixed planes and measurable data (departure (b)). The set of rank-n orthogonal projections of ℝ^N is compact (closed and bounded in End ℝ^N), so there are n-dimensional subspaces Q₁, …, Q_J such that every n-dimensional P has ‖q_P − q_{Qⱼ}‖ < 1/16 for some j. Write qⱼ := q_{Qⱼ} and Kʲ := {z : |qⱼ z| ≤ |z|/3}. If ‖q_P − qⱼ‖ < 1/16 then Kʲ ⊆ K_{1/2}(P), because |q_P z| ≤ |qⱼ z| + |z|/16 ≤ (1/3 + 1/16)|z| < |z|/2.
 For x ∈ ℝ^N, ρ > 0 let m(x, ρ) := μ(B_ρ(x)) and cⱼ(x, ρ) := μ((x + Kʲ) ∩ B_ρ(x)). x ↦ m(x, ρ) is lower semicontinuous (if x_i → x then 1_{B_ρ(x)} ≤ liminf 1_{B_ρ(x_i)} pointwise; Fatou), hence Borel; x ↦ cⱼ(x, ρ) = ∫ 1_{Kʲ ∩ B_ρ(0)}(y − x) dμ(y) is Borel by Tonelli. Both are nondecreasing and left-continuous in ρ (increasing unions as ρ' ↑ ρ). Consequently the quantities Θ_*(x) := liminf_{ρ↓0} m(x,ρ)/(ω_nρⁿ), Θ^*(x) := limsup_{ρ↓0} m(x,ρ)/(ω_nρⁿ), Γⱼ(x) := limsup_{ρ↓0} cⱼ(x,ρ)/ρⁿ can be computed along rational ρ (for rationals r₁ < ρ < r₂: m(x,r₁)/r₂ⁿ ≤ m(x,ρ)/ρⁿ ≤ m(x,r₂)/r₁ⁿ and r₂/r₁ → 1; same for cⱼ), so they are Borel functions of x.
 Let G be a Borel set with μ(ℝ^N ∖ G) = 0 such that (H) holds at every x ∈ G (the exceptional set is μ-null, hence contained in a Borel μ-null set). For x ∈ G, (5') gives Θ_*(x) = Θ^*(x) = θ_x ∈ (0, ∞), and (6') with the inclusion above gives Γⱼ(x) = 0 for every j with ‖q_{P_x} − qⱼ‖ < 1/16. For j ∈ {1..J} and k ∈ ℤ let
 G_{j,k} := {x ∈ G : 2^k ≤ Θ_*(x) = Θ^*(x) < 2^{k+1}, Γⱼ(x) = 0} (Borel).
 Then G = ⋃_{j,k} G_{j,k}. It suffices to find, for each (j, k), a countable union R_{j,k} of closed Lipschitz graphs (closed sets of the form Φ(ℝⁿ) with Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N Lipschitz) with μ(G_{j,k} ∖ R_{j,k}) = 0: then R := ⋃_{j,k} R_{j,k} is Borel and countably n-rectifiable, and μ(ℝ^N ∖ R) ≤ μ(ℝ^N ∖ G) + Σ μ(G_{j,k} ∖ R_{j,k}) = 0.

5. Key lemma (Simon (9)-(10), lines 212-249, corrected; departure (a)). Fix (j, k), put ε := 1/(2(1 + 32ⁿ)), and let E be a set and δ > 0 such that for all x ∈ E and 0 < ρ < δ:
 (9a) m(x, ρ) ≥ (1 − ε) 2^k ω_n ρⁿ, (9b) cⱼ(x, ρ) ≤ ε 2^k ω_n ρⁿ.
 Claim (10'): if x, y ∈ E and 0 < |y − x| < δ/2 then |qⱼ(y − x)| > |y − x|/4.
 Proof. Suppose ρ := |y − x| ∈ (0, δ/2) and |qⱼ(y − x)| ≤ ρ/4. For z ∈ B_{ρ/16}(y): |qⱼ(z − x)| ≤ ρ/4 + ρ/16 = 5ρ/16 and |z − x| ≥ 15ρ/16, so |qⱼ(z − x)| ≤ |z − x|/3, i.e. z ∈ x + Kʲ; also |z − x| < 17ρ/16 < 2ρ. Hence B_{ρ/16}(y) ⊆ (x + Kʲ) ∩ B_{2ρ}(x) and m(y, ρ/16) ≤ cⱼ(x, 2ρ). Since ρ/16 < δ and 2ρ < δ, (9a) at y and (9b) at x give (1 − ε)2^kω_n(ρ/16)ⁿ ≤ ε2^kω_n(2ρ)ⁿ, i.e. 1 − ε ≤ 32ⁿ ε, contradicting ε < 1/(1 + 32ⁿ). ∎

6. Lipschitz graphs (Simon lines 249-262). Let E, δ be as in Step 5 with E compact, and x₀ ∈ E, S := E ∩ B_{δ/4}(x₀). For distinct y, y' ∈ S, |y − y'| < δ/2, so |qⱼ y − qⱼ y'| > |y − y'|/4 by (10'). Hence qⱼ|S is injective and F : qⱼ(S) → Qⱼ^⊥, F(qⱼ y) := y − qⱼ y, satisfies |F(w) − F(w')| ≤ |y − y'| < 4|w − w'|. Extend F to a Lipschitz F̃ : Qⱼ → Qⱼ^⊥ (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.2, applied to each coordinate in an orthonormal basis of Qⱼ^⊥; constant ≤ 4√ℓ). With a linear isometry ι : ℝⁿ → Qⱼ, Φ(w) := ι(w) + F̃(ι(w)) is Lipschitz ℝⁿ → ℝ^N, Γ := Φ(ℝⁿ) = {w + F̃(w) : w ∈ Qⱼ} is closed (if wᵢ + F̃(wᵢ) → z then wᵢ = qⱼ(wᵢ + F̃(wᵢ)) → qⱼ z and z = qⱼ z + F̃(qⱼ z)), countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_range), and S ⊆ Γ (y = qⱼ y + F(qⱼ y)). 7. Egoroff step (Simon (4), (7), (8), lines 168-219). Let T ⊆ G_{j,k} be Borel with μ(T) > 0. Claim: there is a closed finite union Γ of Lipschitz graphs with μ(T ∖ Γ) ≤ μ(T)/2. Proof. For i ≥ 1 and x ∈ ℝ^N let fᵢ(x) := inf{m(x, ρ)/(ω_nρⁿ) : ρ ∈ ℚ ∩ (0, 1/i)}, gᵢ(x) := sup{cⱼ(x, ρ)/(ω_nρⁿ) : ρ ∈ ℚ ∩ (0, 1/i)} (Borel, [0, ∞]-valued). fᵢ < ∞ everywhere as μ is finite. gᵢ < ∞ on T: for x ∈ T, Γⱼ(x) = 0 gives some ρ₀(x) > 0 with cⱼ(x, ρ) ≤ ω_nρⁿ for ρ < ρ₀(x), and cⱼ(x, ρ)/(ω_nρⁿ) ≤ μ(ℝ^N)/(ω_nρ₀(x)ⁿ) for ρ ≥ ρ₀(x) (note gᵢ may be +∞ at atoms of μ outside T, since 0 ∈ Kʲ). On T, fᵢ ↑ Θ_* (finite) and gᵢ ↓ Γⱼ/ω_n = 0. By Egoroff's theorem (μ finite; Mathlib tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto applied to the real-valued restrictions to T) there is a Borel T' ⊆ T with μ(T ∖ T') ≤ μ(T)/4 on which both convergences are uniform; hence there is i₀ with fᵢ₀ ≥ Θ_* − ε2^k ≥ (1 − ε)2^k and gᵢ₀ ≤ ε2^k on T'. By inner regularity of the finite Borel measure μ there is a compact E ⊆ T' with μ(T' ∖ E) ≤ μ(T)/4. With δ := 1/i₀, (9a) and (9b) hold on E for every real ρ ∈ (0, δ): for (9a) use m(x, ρ) ≥ m(x, r) for rationals r ↑ ρ; for (9b) use cⱼ(x, ρ) ≤ cⱼ(x, r') for rationals r' ↓ ρ with r' < δ. Step 6 gives Γ ⊇ E, so μ(T ∖ Γ) ≤ μ(T ∖ T') + μ(T' ∖ E) ≤ μ(T)/2. ∎

8. Exhaustion (Simon lines 263-274, departure (d)). Fix (j, k). Put T₀ := G_{j,k}; if μ(T_t) > 0, Step 7 gives Γ^{(t)} with μ(T_t ∖ Γ^{(t)}) ≤ μ(T_t)/2, and set T_{t+1} := T_t ∖ Γ^{(t)} (Borel); if μ(T_t) = 0 put Γ^{(t)} := ∅, T_{t+1} := T_t. Then μ(T_t) ≤ 2^{-t}μ(G_{j,k}) → 0 and G_{j,k} ∖ ⋃_t Γ^{(t)} ⊆ T_t for all t, so R_{j,k} := ⋃_t Γ^{(t)} satisfies μ(G_{j,k} ∖ R_{j,k}) = 0. By Step 4 this proves the theorem. ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to finite μ by restricting to balls B_k(0) (tangent condition is local).
Trivial cases ℓ = 0 (R = ℝ^N) and n = 0 (μ is carried by its countably many atoms).
From the tangent condition: density lim μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) = θ_x and vanishing cone density around the normal space (Remark 1.5(3)).
Measurable reformulation with finitely many fixed planes Qⱼ (1/16-net) and dyadic density classes G_{j,k}.

Hence such sets are locally Lipschitz graphs over Qⱼ (McShane/Lipschitz extension); compactness gives finitely many graphs.

subproblem.title: Theorem 3.6 (Besicovitch-Federer): purely unrectifiable σ-finite sets have null projections for a.e. projection
subproblem.statement: For n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, N := n + ℓ: if Q ⊆ ℝ^N is purely n-unrectifiable (every countably n-rectifiable subset is Hⁿ-null) and Q = ⋃ⱼ Qⱼ with Hⁿ(Qⱼ) < ∞, then ForAlmostAllProjections N n (fun p ↦ Hⁿ(p(Q)) = 0), i.e. for Lebesgue-a.e. v ∈ (ℝ^N)ⁿ with v linearly independent, Hⁿ(p_v(Q)) = 0 where p_v = frameProjection v is the orthogonal projection onto span v.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source and departure. Simon, Ch. 3, Theorem 3.6 (chapter-03.txt lines 530-536, printed p. 80) gives no proof: “For the proof of this theorem see [Fed69] or [Ros84]” (line 536). The printed argument is therefore incomplete (absent), and we supply the standard proof of the Besicovitch-Federer projection theorem from P. Mattila, Geometry of Sets and Measures in Euclidean Spaces (CUP 1995), Ch. 15 (cone criteria) and Ch. 18 (Theorem 18.1), in the presentation of M. G. Dall'Alba, The Besicovitch-Federer Projection Theorem (Master's thesis, Padova 2020, https://www.math.unipd.it/~monti/tesi/DallAlba.pdf), Lemmas 4.5-4.7, 4.15-4.16, 5.2-5.6 and the proof of Theorem 5.1; cf. [Fed69, §3.3]. Two adaptations: (a) the reduction from σ-finite, possibly non-measurable Q to compact purely unrectifiable sets (Step 1), using SimonGMT's measurable form of Lemma 3.2 (not the sibling, to avoid a dependency cycle); (b) the contract encodes “σ-a.e. p ∈ O(n+ℓ, n)” as “Lebesgue-a.e. linearly independent frame v ∈ (ℝ^{n+ℓ})ⁿ, p = orthogonal projection onto span v” (ForAlmostAllProjections, frameProjection); Step 9 transfers the Haar-measure statement to frames.

Notation. N := n + ℓ, ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), Hⁿ = μHE[n], B(a, r) open ball, ω_n = Lⁿ(B(0,1)). For an ℓ-dimensional subspace V (“the fibre direction”), W := V^⊥ (n-dimensional) and Q_V := orthogonal projection onto W (so Q_V = frameProjection v when W = span v). Hⁿ restricted to an n-plane is its Lebesgue measure; Q_V is 1-Lipschitz. Cones: for a ∈ ℝ^N, 0 < s < 1, r > 0,
 X(a, V, s) := {x : |Q_V(x − a)| < s|x − a|} (an open cone around a + V, not containing a), X(a, r, V, s) := X(a, V, s) ∩ B(a, r).
Note Q_V(X(a, r, V, s)) ⊆ W ∩ B(Q_V a, rs). O(N) denotes the orthogonal group (a compact metrizable group) and θ_N its Haar probability measure, which is left and right invariant (compact groups are unimodular).

Statement. If Q ⊆ ℝ^N is purely n-unrectifiable and Q = ⋃ⱼ Qⱼ with Hⁿ(Qⱼ) < ∞, then for Lebesgue-a.e. v ∈ (ℝ^N)ⁿ with v linearly independent, Hⁿ(frameProjection v '' Q) = 0.

Proof.

0. Trivial cases. If n = 0: any x ∈ Q gives the countably 0-rectifiable subset {x} (range of a constant map ℝ⁰ → ℝ^N) with H⁰({x}) = 1 > 0, so Q = ∅ and the claim is trivial. If ℓ = 0: Q ⊆ ℝⁿ = range(id) is countably n-rectifiable, so Hⁿ(Q) = 0 by pure unrectifiability and Hⁿ(p(Q)) ≤ Hⁿ(Q) = 0 for every 1-Lipschitz p. Assume n ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 1.

1. Reduction to compact sets (adaptation (a)). For each j choose a Borel Bⱼ ⊇ Qⱼ with Hⁿ(Bⱼ) = Hⁿ(Qⱼ) < ∞ (Borel regularity; Mathlib toMeasurable). By the measurable case of Lemma 3.2 (SimonGMT Chapter03.measurable_rectifiable_purelyUnrectifiable_decomposition), Bⱼ = Rⱼ ∪ Pⱼ with Rⱼ Borel and countably n-rectifiable and Pⱼ Hⁿ-measurable and purely n-unrectifiable. Qⱼ ∩ Rⱼ ⊆ Q is countably rectifiable, so Hⁿ(Qⱼ ∩ Rⱼ) = 0 (Q is purely unrectifiable). By inner regularity of the finite Borel regular measure Hⁿ⌞Bⱼ (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15(2), 1.16) Pⱼ contains a countable union of compact sets K_{j,i} with Hⁿ(Pⱼ ∖ ⋃ᵢ K_{j,i}) = 0. Thus Q ⊆ Z ∪ ⋃_{j,i} K_{j,i} with Hⁿ(Z) = 0 and each K_{j,i} compact, purely n-unrectifiable (⊆ Pⱼ) with Hⁿ(K_{j,i}) < ∞. As every Q_V is 1-Lipschitz, Hⁿ(Q_V(Z)) = 0 for every V. A countable intersection of full-measure sets of frames has full measure, so it suffices to prove: for every compact, purely n-unrectifiable A ⊆ ℝ^N with Hⁿ(A) < ∞, Hⁿ(frameProjection v '' A) = 0 for Lebesgue-a.e. linearly independent v. Fix such A for Steps 2-10.

2. Cone-free sets are rectifiable (Mattila 15.13; Dall'Alba Lemma 4.5). Let V, 0 < s < 1, r ∈ (0, ∞] and E ⊆ ℝ^N with E ∩ X(a, r, V, s) = ∅ for all a ∈ E. Then E is countably n-rectifiable. Proof: cover E by countably many sets Eᵢ of diameter < r. For a, b ∈ Eᵢ, |b − a| < r and b ∉ X(a, r, V, s) give |Q_V(b − a)| ≥ s|b − a|; so Q_V|Eᵢ is injective with (1/s)-Lipschitz inverse Q_V(Eᵢ) → Eᵢ. Extend this inverse to a Lipschitz map W → ℝ^N (Simon Ch. 2, 1.2, coordinatewise) and precompose with a linear isometry ℝⁿ → W: Eᵢ is contained in the range of a Lipschitz map ℝⁿ → ℝ^N.

3. Small cone mass forces small mass (Mattila 15.14; Dall'Alba Lemma 4.6, constants adjusted). Let V, 0 < s < 1, δ > 0, λ > 0 and let B ⊆ ℝ^N be purely n-unrectifiable with Hⁿ(B ∩ X(x, r, V, s)) ≤ λ rⁿ sⁿ for all x ∈ B and 0 < r < δ. Then Hⁿ(B ∩ B(a, δ/8)) ≤ 2·15ⁿ λ δⁿ for every a ∈ ℝ^N.
 Proof. Let B' := B ∩ B(a, δ/8) and B'' := {x ∈ B' : B' ∩ X(x, V, s/4) ≠ ∅}. The set E := B' ∖ B'' satisfies E ∩ X(x, V, s/4) = ∅ for x ∈ E, so it is countably rectifiable by Step 2 (r = ∞), hence Hⁿ(E) = 0 (E ⊆ B); so Hⁿ(B') = Hⁿ(B''). For x ∈ B'' let h(x) := sup{|y − x| : y ∈ B' ∩ X(x, V, s/4)} ∈ (0, δ/4] and pick x' ∈ B' ∩ X(x, V, s/4) with |x' − x| ≥ 3h(x)/4. Let C_x := {z : |Q_V(z − x)| < s h(x)/4}. Claim: B' ∩ C_x ⊆ {x} ∪ X(x, 3h(x), V, s) ∪ X(x', 3h(x), V, s). Let z ∈ B' ∩ C_x, z ≠ x. If |z − x| > h(x) then |Q_V(z − x)| < s h(x)/4 < (s/4)|z − x|, i.e. z ∈ B' ∩ X(x, V, s/4), contradicting the definition of h(x); so |z − x| ≤ h(x) and |z − x'| ≤ 2h(x) < 3h(x). If z = x', then z ∈ X(x, 3h(x), V, s) because x' ∈ X(x, V, s/4) ⊆ X(x, V, s) and |x' − x| ≤ h(x). If z ∈ X(x', V, s), then z ∈ X(x', 3h(x), V, s) because |z − x'| < 3h(x). Otherwise z ≠ x' and z ∉ X(x', V, s), i.e. s|z − x'| ≤ |Q_V(z − x')| ≤ |Q_V(z − x)| + |Q_V(x − x')| < s h(x)/4 + (s/4)|x − x'| ≤ s h(x)/2; then |z − x'| < h(x)/2, so |z − x| > 3h(x)/4 − h(x)/2 = h(x)/4 > |Q_V(z − x)|/s, i.e. z ∈ X(x, V, s), and |z − x| ≤ h(x) < 3h(x), so z ∈ X(x, 3h(x), V, s). Since x, x' ∈ B and 3h(x) ≤ 3δ/4 < δ, the hypothesis gives Hⁿ(B' ∩ C_x) ≤ 2λ(3h(x))ⁿsⁿ (n ≥ 1, so {x} is null). The balls W ∩ B(Q_V x, s h(x)/20), x ∈ B'', have bounded radii; by the 5r-covering lemma (Simon Ch. 1, 3.4) there are countably many xᵢ ∈ B'' with these balls pairwise disjoint and Q_V(B'') ⊆ ⋃ᵢ W ∩ B(Q_V xᵢ, s h(xᵢ)/4); hence B'' ⊆ ⋃ᵢ C_{xᵢ}. The disjoint balls lie in W ∩ B(Q_V a, δ/8 + δ/80) ⊆ W ∩ B(Q_V a, δ/4). Therefore Hⁿ(B') ≤ Σᵢ 2λ 3ⁿ sⁿ h(xᵢ)ⁿ = 2λ 60ⁿ ω_n⁻¹ Σᵢ Hⁿ(W ∩ B(Q_V xᵢ, s h(xᵢ)/20)) ≤ 2λ 60ⁿ (δ/4)ⁿ = 2·15ⁿ λ δⁿ. ∎

4. Cone density is positive a.e. (Mattila 15.15-15.16; Dall'Alba Corollary 4.7). For every V and δ > 0, for Hⁿ-a.e. a ∈ A: Φ_δ(a, V) := limsup_{s↓0} sup_{0<r<δ} (rs)^{-n} Hⁿ(A ∩ X(a, r, V, s)) > 0.
 Proof. Let Z be the set where Φ_δ(a, V) = 0. Fix λ > 0 and for i ∈ ℕ let Zᵢ := {a ∈ Z : sup_{0<r<δ}(rs)^{-n}Hⁿ(A ∩ X(a, r, V, s)) ≤ λ for all s ∈ (0, 1/i)}. Then Zᵢ ↑ and ⋃ᵢ Zᵢ = Z. For fixed i and s ∈ (0, 1/i), B := Zᵢ ⊆ A is purely unrectifiable and Hⁿ(B ∩ X(x, r, V, s)) ≤ Hⁿ(A ∩ X(x, r, V, s)) ≤ λ rⁿ sⁿ for x ∈ B, r < δ; Step 3 gives Hⁿ(Zᵢ ∩ B(a, δ/8)) ≤ 2·15ⁿλδⁿ for all a. Letting i → ∞ (continuity from below of the outer measure Hⁿ along increasing sequences, Borel regularity) and then λ ↓ 0: Hⁿ(Z ∩ B(a, δ/8)) = 0 for all a; countably many such balls cover ℝ^N, so Hⁿ(Z) = 0. ∎

5. First exceptional set (Dall'Alba Lemma 5.2). A_{1,δ}(V) := {a ∈ A : Φ_δ(a, V) = 0} has Hⁿ(A_{1,δ}(V)) = 0, by Step 4.

6. Second exceptional set (Dall'Alba Lemma 5.3). A_{2,δ}(V) := {a ∈ A : Φ_δ(a, V) = ∞} has Hⁿ(Q_V(A_{2,δ}(V))) = 0.
 Proof. Fix K > 0. Each a ∈ A_{2,δ}(V) admits arbitrarily small s > 0 and some r ∈ (0, δ) with Hⁿ(A ∩ X(a, r, V, s)) ≥ K(rs)ⁿ; the closed balls W ∩ B̄(Q_V a, rs) (radius rs < δs, arbitrarily small) form a fine cover of Q_V(A_{2,δ}(V)). By the Vitali covering theorem for Lebesgue (outer) measure on the n-plane W (Simon Ch. 1, Remark 3.11 / Symmetric Vitali Property; Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_covering_ae) there are countably many pairwise disjoint such balls W ∩ B̄(Q_V aᵢ, rᵢsᵢ) covering Hⁿ-almost all of Q_V(A_{2,δ}(V)). The sets A ∩ X(aᵢ, rᵢ, V, sᵢ) are Borel and pairwise disjoint (their Q_V-images lie in the disjoint balls), so Hⁿ(Q_V(A_{2,δ}(V))) ≤ Σᵢ ω_n(rᵢsᵢ)ⁿ ≤ (ω_n/K)Σᵢ Hⁿ(A ∩ X(aᵢ, rᵢ, V, sᵢ)) ≤ ω_n Hⁿ(A)/K. Let K → ∞. ∎

7. Third exceptional set (Dall'Alba Lemma 5.4). A₃(V) := {a ∈ A : A ∩ (a + V) is infinite} has Hⁿ(Q_V(A₃(V))) = 0.
 Proof. Let ι : ℝⁿ → W be a linear isometry and f := ι⁻¹∘Q_V : ℝ^N → ℝⁿ (1-Lipschitz). The sibling eilenberg_inequality (with m := n, k := 0) gives a Borel g ≥ H⁰(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) with ∫ g dLⁿ ≤ C·Hⁿ(A) < ∞, so H⁰(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) < ∞ for Lⁿ-a.e. y. For a ∈ A₃(V), f⁻¹{f(a)} = a + V, so f(A₃(V)) ⊆ {g = ∞}, an Lⁿ-null set, and Q_V(A₃(V)) = ι(f(A₃(V))) is Hⁿ-null. ∎

8. The key lemma (Mattila Ch. 18; Dall'Alba Lemma 5.6). For δ > 0 and V let A_{3,δ}(V) := {a ∈ A : (A ∖ {a}) ∩ (a + V) ∩ B(a, δ) ≠ ∅}, and say that the trichotomy T_δ(a, V) holds if Φ_δ(a, V) ∈ {0, ∞} or a ∈ A_{3,δ}(V). Claim: for θ_N-a.e. g ∈ O(N), and also (Step 9) for Lebesgue-a.e. frame v, Hⁿ({a ∈ A : not T_δ(a, V)}) = 0, where V = gV₀ (V₀ := span{e_{n+1}, …, e_N}), resp. V = (span v)^⊥.
 8a. Measurability. Parametrize V by the projection Q = Q_V (a continuous function of g, and of v on the open set of independent frames: Q = v(vᵀv)⁻¹vᵀ). The indicator of {(x, a, Q, r, s) : |Q(x − a)| < s|x − a|, |x − a| < r} is lower semicontinuous, so (a, Q, r, s) ↦ Hⁿ(A ∩ X(a, r, V, s)) is lower semicontinuous (Fatou, Hⁿ⌞A finite) hence Borel; it is nondecreasing and left-continuous in r and in s, so the sup over r ∈ (0, δ) and the limsup over s ↓ 0 may be taken along rationals (for rationals s₁ < s < s₂, (rs₂)^{-n}Hⁿ(…s₁) ≤ (rs)^{-n}Hⁿ(…s) ≤ (rs₁)^{-n}Hⁿ(…s₂)), and (a, Q) ↦ Φ_δ(a, V) is Borel. The set {(a, Q) : a ∈ A_{3,δ}(V)} is the projection of the σ-compact set ⋃_j{(a, Q, b) ∈ A × 𝒬 × A : 1/j ≤ |b − a| ≤ δ − 1/j, (I − Q)(b − a) = b − a} (𝒬 the compact set of rank-n orthogonal projections), hence σ-compact. So (a, Q) ↦ T_δ(a, V) is Borel.
 8b. Sphere lemma (Dall'Alba Theorem 4.16 and first part of the proof of 5.6). Let H ⊆ ℝ^N be an (n+1)-dimensional subspace, S(H) its unit sphere (≅ Sⁿ, with the measure Hⁿ⌞S(H)), p_H the orthogonal projection onto H, and for θ ∈ S(H), 0 < s < 1: Z_{H,θ}(s) := {x : dist(p_H x, ℝθ) < s|p_H x|} (“slab cone” with axis ℝθ ⊕ H^⊥). Let A' ⊆ ℝ^N be compact with Hⁿ(A') < ∞ and say (H, θ) is good for A' if Ψ(θ) := limsup_{s↓0} sup_{0<r<δ}(rs)^{-n}Hⁿ(A' ∩ B(0, r) ∩ Z_{H,θ}(s)) ∈ {0, ∞} or (A' ∖ {0}) ∩ B(0, δ) ∩ (ℝθ ⊕ H^⊥) ≠ ∅. Claim: for Hⁿ-a.e. θ ∈ S(H), (H, θ) is good for A'.
 Proof. For E ⊆ S(H) let Λ(E) := {x : p_H x ≠ 0, p_H x/|p_H x| ∈ E or −p_H x/|p_H x| ∈ E} and μ(E) := sup_{0<r<δ} r^{-n}Hⁿ(A' ∩ B(0, r) ∩ Λ(E)); μ is an outer measure on S(H) (Λ(∅) = ∅, Λ commutes with unions, and a supremum of countably subadditive monotone set functions is countably subadditive and monotone). Hence μ(S(H) ∖ C) = 0. Density dichotomy (Dall'Alba Lemma 4.15 and Theorem 4.16, on the sphere): for every Borel F ⊆ S(H) with μ(F) = 0, for Hⁿ-a.e. θ ∈ F, limsup_{t↓0} t^{-n}μ(S(H) ∩ B(θ, t)) ∈ {0, ∞}.  8c. From slab cones to cones (Dall'Alba Lemma 5.5, generalized). Let V be ℓ-dimensional with orthonormal basis u₁, …, u_ℓ, W = V^⊥, H_j := W ⊕ ℝu_j.  8d. Averaging over O(N) (Dall'Alba, proof of 5.6, second part). Fix a ∈ A and put A' := A − a (compact); T_δ(a, V) for A is T_δ(0, V) for A'. For g ∈ O(N) use V = gV₀ with basis u_j = g e_{n+j}, so (H_j, u_j) = (gH⁰_j, ge_{n+j}), H⁰_j := span{e₁, …, e_n, e_{n+j}}. 9. Transfer to frames (adaptation (b)). Applying this to 𝒢_δ := {V : Hⁿ({a ∈ A : not T_δ(a, V)}) > 0} (Borel in the projection Q_V by 8a and Tonelli) gives: for Lebesgue-a.e. independent v, Hⁿ({a ∈ A : not T_δ(a, (span v)^⊥)}) = 0.

10. Conclusion (Dall'Alba, proof of Theorem 5.1). Let v be independent and outside the null sets of Step 9 for all δ = 1/i, i ≥ 1; V := (span v)^⊥, so Q_V = frameProjection v. Put Gᵢ := {a ∈ A : not T_{1/i}(a, V)} (Hⁿ-null). With Step 1 this proves ForAlmostAllProjections (n+ℓ) n (fun p ↦ Hⁿ(p '' Q) = 0). ∎
proof_key_steps: Trivial cases n = 0 (Q = ∅) and ℓ = 0 (Hⁿ(Q) = 0).
Reduce to compact purely unrectifiable A with Hⁿ(A) < ∞ (Borel hulls, SimonGMT measurable Lemma 3.2, inner regularity).
Cone lemmas (Mattila 15.13-15.16): cone-free sets are rectifiable; hence the cone density Φ_δ(a, V) > 0 at a.e. a.
Exceptional sets: {Φ_δ = ∞} has null projection (Vitali covering); {A ∩ (a+V) infinite} has null projection (sibling Eilenberg, k = 0).

Key lemma: for a.e. V the trichotomy (Φ_δ ∈ {0, ∞} or a point of A in a + V near a) holds at a.e. a — via the sphere density dichotomy for slab cones, slab-to-cone inclusions, and averaging over O(N) with Haar measure.
Transfer from Haar-a.e. g ∈ O(N) to Lebesgue-a.e. frames by O(N)-invariance of Lebesgue measure and right invariance of Haar measure.
Combine over δ = 1/i: A is covered by null sets, sets with null projection, and A₃(V).

subproblem.title: Lemma 1.2: countable rectifiability via C¹ submanifold covers
subproblem.statement: For all n, ℓ ∈ ℕ and M ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ}: M is countably n-rectifiable (M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃ⱼ Fⱼ(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and Fⱼ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+ℓ} Lipschitz) if and only if there are N₀ ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with Hⁿ(N₀) = 0 and sets N_j (j ∈ ℕ), each an n-dimensional embedded C¹ submanifold in the sense of IsC1Submanifold n (Simon Ch. 2 (4.1): local injective C¹ parametrizations ψ : V → W with ψ(V) = W ∩ N_j, relatively proper, with injective derivative), such that M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_j N_j.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2, chapter-03.txt lines 25-65 (printed pp. 69-70), with Definition 1.1 (lines 13-23) and the definition of an embedded C¹ submanifold, Ch. 2 (4.1) (chapter-02.txt lines 849-860), transcribed in the contract as IsC1Submanifold. Errata corrected (all in the printed proof, lines 39-65): (i) “G_1j, G_2j, … : ℝⁿ → ℝ^ℓ” should read “ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+ℓ}”; (ii) display (1) “graph F_j ⊂ E_j ∩ (∪ᵢ G_ij(ℝⁿ))” should read “F_j(ℝⁿ) ⊂ E_j ∪ (∪ᵢ G_ij(ℝⁿ))”; (iii) the incomplete sentence “by the area formula Lⁿ({x : J_{G_ij} = 0}” should read “by the area formula Hⁿ(G_ij({x : J_{G_ij}(x) = 0})) = 0”; (iv) “submanifold of ℝⁿ” should read “of ℝ^{n+ℓ}”; (v) to obtain an *embedded* submanifold in the sense of (4.1) (properness), σ must be chosen so that G_ij is injective on the closed ball B̄_σ(x) (Step 7 below; we use B̄_{2σ}(x), which is harmless).

Notation. ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), N = n + ℓ, Hⁿ = μHE[n], Lⁿ = volume = Hⁿ on ℝⁿ. For a C¹ map G : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N, JG(x) := normDet(DG(x)) = √det(DG(x)*DG(x)); JG(x) = 0 iff DG(x) is not injective.

Statement. For all n, ℓ and M ⊆ ℝ^N: CountablyRectifiable n M ⟺ ∃ N₀, (N_j)_{j∈ℕ}: Hⁿ(N₀) = 0, every N_j satisfies IsC1Submanifold n, and M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_j N_j.

Proof.

1. “⇐” (Simon lines 28-38). SimonGMT proves this direction: Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_of_submanifold_cover (Chapter03/SubmanifoldCover.lean) for submanifolds satisfying Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := ℝⁿ) 1. That predicate unfolds to: 1 ≤ 1 and for every y ∈ N there are V ⊆ ℝⁿ, W ⊆ ℝ^N, φ with y ∈ W, V and W open, φ C¹ on V, φ injective on V, φ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ φ⁻¹(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dφ(x) injective for x ∈ V — exactly the conditions of IsC1Submanifold n N, reordered (the exponent 1 : ℕ∞ coerces to the same smoothness index). For completeness, the argument (Simon lines 28-38): every chart φ is C¹ on the open V, hence Lipschitz on each closed ball contained in V; V is a countable union of such balls; each restriction extends to a Lipschitz map ℝⁿ → ℝ^N (Ch. 2, Theorem 1.2 coordinatewise); by Lindelöf countably many chart images W ∩ N = φ(V) cover N. Hence N is contained in a countable union of Lipschitz images, and M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_j N_j is countably n-rectifiable (N₀ serves as the null set M₀ of Definition 1.1, after merging countably many index families with Nat.pair).

2. “⇒”: setup (Simon lines 39-42). Let M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_{j∈ℕ} F_j(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and F_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N Lipschitz (Definition 1.1).

3. The case n = 0. ℝ⁰ is a point, so each F_j(ℝ⁰) = {p_j} is a single point, and H⁰(M₀) = 0 forces M₀ = ∅ (H⁰ is counting measure). A singleton {p} satisfies IsC1Submanifold 0: take V := ℝ⁰ (open), W := ℝ^N, ψ :≡ p; then y = p ∈ W, ψ is C¹ and injective on the one-point V, ψ(V) = {p} = W ∩ {p}, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) ∈ {∅, V} is compact, and Dψ is injective because its domain is 0-dimensional. Thus N₀ := ∅, N_j := {p_j} works. Assume n ≥ 1.

4. C¹ approximation (Simon lines 39-47). By the sibling theorem c1_approximation (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5), for each j and i ≥ 1 there is a C¹ map G_{ij} : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N with Lⁿ({x : F_j(x) ≠ G_{ij}(x)}) < 1/i. Put Z_j := ℝⁿ ∖ ⋃ᵢ{F_j = G_{ij}}. Then Lⁿ(Z_j) ≤ Lⁿ({F_j ≠ G_{ij}}) < 1/i for every i, so Lⁿ(Z_j) = 0.

5. Null part (Simon lines 47-59, erratum (ii)). If x ∉ Z_j then F_j(x) = G_{ij}(x) for some i, so F_j(ℝⁿ) ⊆ E_j ∪ ⋃ᵢ G_{ij}(ℝⁿ) with E_j := F_j(Z_j). Since F_j is Lipschitz, Hⁿ(E_j) ≤ (Lip F_j)ⁿ Lⁿ(Z_j) = 0 (SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn). Hence with N₀' := M₀ ∪ ⋃_j E_j (Hⁿ-null), M ⊆ N₀' ∪ ⋃_{i,j} G_{ij}(ℝⁿ).

6. Critical images are null (Simon line 61, erratum (iii)). Let G : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N be C¹ and Crit(G) := {x : JG(x) = 0}, a closed set (JG² = det(DG*DG) is continuous; Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_sq, normDet_eq_zero_iff_ker_ne_bot). For k ∈ ℕ, G is Lipschitz on the open ball B_k(0), and the weighted area formula for Lipschitz maps (Simon Ch. 2, (3.4)-(3.5); SimonGMT Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum on s := B_k(0) with weight w := 1_{Crit(G)}; on the open s the Jacobian within s is JG at every point; the source measure μHE[n] on ℝⁿ is volume, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume) gives ∫ #(Crit(G) ∩ B_k(0) ∩ G⁻¹{y}) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{B_k(0)} JG·1_{Crit(G)} dLⁿ = 0. Hence the multiplicity vanishes for Hⁿ-a.e. y, i.e. Hⁿ(G(Crit(G) ∩ B_k(0))) = 0 (y ∈ G(…) iff the multiplicity is ≥ 1). Union over k: Hⁿ(G(Crit(G))) = 0.

7. Regular images are locally embedded submanifolds (Simon lines 61-64, erratum (v)). Let x ∈ ℝⁿ with JG(x) > 0, i.e. DG(x) injective; c := min_{|v|=1}|DG(x)v| > 0. Choose σ > 0 with ‖DG(z) − DG(x)‖ ≤ c/2 for z ∈ B̄_{2σ}(x). By the mean value inequality, |G(z) − G(z') − DG(x)(z − z')| ≤ (c/2)|z − z'| on B̄_{2σ}(x), so |G(z) − G(z')| ≥ (c/2)|z − z'|: G is injective on B̄_{2σ}(x), and DG(z) is injective there (|DG(z)v| ≥ (c/2)|v|). G restricted to the compact B̄_{2σ}(x) is a homeomorphism onto K̂ := G(B̄_{2σ}(x)). Hence N' := G(B_σ(x)) is relatively open in K̂: there is an open W ⊆ ℝ^N with W ∩ K̂ = N'. Claim: IsC1Submanifold n N', with the single chart V := B_σ(x), W, ψ := G at every y ∈ N'. Indeed y ∈ N' ⊆ W; V, W open; G is C¹ and injective on V; G(V) = N' = W ∩ N'; Dψ is injective on V; and properness: let K ⊆ W be compact and z_k ∈ V with G(z_k) ∈ K; pass to a subsequence z_k → z* ∈ B̄_σ(x) ⊆ B̄_{2σ}(x); then G(z*) ∈ K ∩ K̂ ⊆ W ∩ K̂ = N' = G(B_σ(x)), so G(z*) = G(z') with z' ∈ B_σ(x), and injectivity on B̄_{2σ}(x) gives z* = z' ∈ V. Thus V ∩ G⁻¹(K) is sequentially compact, hence compact.

8. Countability (Simon lines 64-65). The set Reg(G) := {JG > 0} is open; by Lindelöf it is covered by countably many balls B_{σ_k}(x_k) as in Step 7, so G(Reg(G)) ⊆ ⋃_k G(B_{σ_k}(x_k)), a countable union of n-dimensional C¹ submanifolds.

9. Conclusion. N₀ := N₀' ∪ ⋃_{i,j} G_{ij}(Crit(G_{ij})) has Hⁿ(N₀) = 0 (countable union of null sets, Steps 5-6), and M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_{i,j,k} G_{ij}(B_{σ_{ijk}}(x_{ijk})) by Steps 5, 7, 8. Enumerate the countable family of submanifolds by ℕ (padding with ∅, which satisfies IsC1Submanifold vacuously, if it is finite). ∎

subproblem.title: Area formula (2.4)-(2.5) for countably n-rectifiable sets
subproblem.statement: For n, ℓ, ℓ₁ ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} Hⁿ-measurable and countably n-rectifiable, θ a positive locally integrable weight on M, U ⊇ M open and f : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ^{n+ℓ₁} locally Lipschitz on U, with T_xM := approxTangentPlane n M θ x and J^M_f(x) := areaJacobian (T_xM) f x = normDet of the tangential differential: (a) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there are P and a continuous linear L : P → ℝ^{n+ℓ₁} with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P and HasTangentialDifferentialAt P f x L; (b) for every Hⁿ-measurable A ⊆ M, ∫_A J^M_f dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝ^{n+ℓ₁}} #(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) dHⁿ(y) (# = encard); (c) for every Hⁿ⌞M-measurable h : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → [0, ∞], ∫_M h·J^M_f dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝ^{n+ℓ₁}} Σ_{x ∈ M ∩ f⁻¹{y}} h(x) dHⁿ(y). (This is the contract's AreaFormula; outer integrals over the target, correcting the printed ℝ^{n+ℓ}.)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 3, (2.1)-(2.6), chapter-03.txt lines 327-409 (printed pp. 75-77): Definitions 2.1-2.3, the area formula 2.4 with its proof (lines 370-396) and 2.5 (lines 397-401). Erratum (README, contract docstring): the outer integrals are over the target ℝ^{n+ℓ₁} (printed ℝ^{n+ℓ} in 2.4/2.5 and ℝⁿ in the display on line 388). Departure: Simon's written proof (lines 377-396) replaces f on M_j by C¹ functions g_j (C¹ approximation) and applies the smooth area formula 3.4 of Ch. 2 on N_j; we follow instead the route Simon states just before it (lines 370-371: “In view of 4.11 and the area formula for Lipschitz maps from domains in ℝⁿ, as discussed in §3, we have the general area formula”), i.e. the Lipschitz area formula on parameter domains plus the Jacobian chain rule (4.11) of Ch. 2; this avoids extending C¹ functions off the submanifolds. The identification T_xM = T_xN_j a.e. (Remark 1.5(2), line 348) and the tangential differential (Ch. 2 (4.8)-(4.10)) are supplied by the sibling chart_tangent_differential.

Notation. N = n + ℓ, P := n + ℓ₁ (target dimension), ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^N and on ℝ^P, Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ. For x ∈ M: T_xM := approxTangentPlane n M θ x, d^Mf_x := tangentialDifferential T_xM f x, J^M_f(x) := areaJacobian T_xM f x = normDet(d^Mf_x). #S := S.encard ∈ [0, ∞] (H⁰ = counting measure). For a C¹ map ψ, Jψ(u) := normDet(Dψ(u)).

Statement. AreaFormula: for M Hⁿ-measurable and countably n-rectifiable, θ a positive locally integrable weight on M, U ⊇ M open, f locally Lipschitz on U: (a) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there are P and L : P →L ℝ^P with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P and HasTangentialDifferentialAt P f x L; (b) ∫_A J^M_f dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝ^P} #(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) dHⁿ(y) for every Hⁿ-measurable A ⊆ M; (c) ∫_M h·J^M_f dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝ^P} Σ_{x∈M∩f⁻¹{y}} h(x) dHⁿ(y) for every Hⁿ⌞M-measurable h : ℝ^N → [0, ∞].

Proof.

1. Good chart balls. By the sibling submanifold_cover (Lemma 1.2), M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_j N_j with Hⁿ(N₀) = 0 and IsC1Submanifold n N_j, and (Lindelöf, as the chart targets W are open and ℝ^N is second countable) each N_j is a countable union of chart images ψ(V), with V ⊆ ℝⁿ open, ψ C¹ and injective on V, Dψ(u) injective for u ∈ V. For such a chart and u ∈ V with ψ(u) ∈ U, choose a closed ball D = B̄_r(u) ⊆ V such that (i) ψ is bi-Lipschitz on D (if n = 0 then D = {u} = ℝ⁰ and (i) is vacuous; otherwise): with c := min_{|v|=1}|Dψ(u)v| > 0 and r so small that ‖Dψ(z) − Dψ(u)‖ ≤ c/2 on D, the mean value inequality gives (c/2)|z − z'| ≤ |ψ(z) − ψ(z')| ≤ (‖Dψ(u)‖ + c/2)|z − z'|; (ii) ψ(D) ⊆ B_s(ψ(u)) ⊆ U where f is Lipschitz on B_s(ψ(u)) (f is locally Lipschitz on the open U). The open set V ∩ ψ⁻¹(U) is covered by the interiors of such balls, hence by countably many of them (Lindelöf). Collecting over all charts we obtain countably many pairs (ψ_α, D_α), α ∈ ℕ (pad with D_α = ∅ if needed), with: ψ_α C¹ on an open set containing the compact ball D_α, injective and bi-Lipschitz on D_α, Dψ_α(z) injective on D_α, h_α := f∘ψ_α Lipschitz on D_α, and M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_α ψ_α(int D_α) (every x ∈ M ∖ N₀ is ψ(u) for a chart with ψ(u) = x ∈ M ⊆ U).

2. Pointwise identification (Simon (2.1)-(2.3), lines 337-370; Ch. 2 (4.11)). Apply the sibling chart_tangent_differential to (M, U, θ, f) and the chart underlying α (V open, ψ C¹ on V, Dψ injective on V). It gives an Lⁿ-null Z_α such that every u ∈ D_α ∖ Z_α with x := ψ_α(u) ∈ M satisfies: (A) HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T_u, T_u := range Dψ_α(u); (B) h_α is differentiable at u; (C) HasLineDerivAt ℝ f (Dh_α(u)w) x (Dψ_α(u)w) for all w. Consequences at such u:
 (a') T_xM = T_u: the predicate ∃P, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P holds, so approxTangentPlane chooses some P' with this property, and P' = T_u by uniqueness (SimonGMT HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, applicable as θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M).
 (b') Let L_x : T_u → ℝ^P be the linear map L_x(Dψ_α(u)w) := Dh_α(u)w (well defined: Dψ_α(u) : ℝⁿ → T_u is a linear isomorphism; continuous as T_u is finite dimensional). By (C), HasTangentialDifferentialAt T_u f x L_x. Line derivatives are unique, so every L' with HasTangentialDifferentialAt T_u f x L' equals L_x; hence d^Mf_x = tangentialDifferential T_u f x = L_x.
 (c') Jacobian chain rule (Simon Ch. 2 (4.11)): Dh_α(u) = L_x ∘ Dψ_α(u), so by Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_comp (equivalently SimonGMT Chapter02.areaJacobian_comp_eq_parametrization_mul_tangential, with any linear extension of L_x to ℝ^N), normDet(Dh_α(u)) = normDet(L_x)·normDet(Dψ_α(u)), i.e. Jh_α(u) = J^M_f(ψ_α(u))·Jψ_α(u).
 Conclusion (a): the set N₀ ∪ ⋃_α ψ_α(Z_α ∩ D_α) is Hⁿ-null (ψ_α is Lipschitz on D_α, and Lⁿ = Hⁿ on ℝⁿ by EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume); every x ∈ M outside it is ψ_α(u) with u ∈ int D_α ∖ Z_α, and P := T_u, L := L_x satisfy (a).

3. Decomposition of A. Let A ⊆ M be Hⁿ-measurable. Put A_α := (A ∩ ψ_α(D_α)) ∖ ⋃_{β<α} ψ_β(D_β) and A_∞ := A ∖ ⋃_α ψ_α(D_α) ⊆ N₀. The A_α are pairwise disjoint and Hⁿ-measurable (the ψ_β(D_β) are compact), A = A_∞ ⊔ ⨆_α A_α, Hⁿ(A_∞) = 0. Let B_α := D_α ∩ ψ_α⁻¹(A_α); ψ_α : B_α → A_α is a bijection, and B_α is Lⁿ-measurable (A_α is a Borel set plus an Hⁿ-null set; ψ_α|D_α is a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism onto a compact set, so preimages of Borel sets are Borel and of Hⁿ-null sets are Lⁿ-null).

4. Measurability of J^M_f. By (c'), for u ∈ B_α ∖ Z_α: J^M_f(ψ_α(u)) = Jh_α(u)/Jψ_α(u), and the right side is an Lⁿ-measurable function on B_α (u ↦ Dh_α(u) is measurable where defined, Mathlib measurable_fderiv; Jψ_α is continuous and positive on D_α). Transporting by the bi-Lipschitz ψ_α, J^M_f agrees Hⁿ-a.e. on A_α with a Borel function; hence J^M_f is Hⁿ⌞A-measurable (A_∞ is null).

5. One piece (Simon lines 385-390). The area formula for the Lipschitz map h_α on the Lⁿ-measurable set B_α (Simon Ch. 2 (3.4); SimonGMT Chapter02.area_formula_lipschitzOn_multiplicity, whose Jacobian is normDet of the derivative within B_α, equal to Jh_α(u) at Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ B_α) gives ∫_{ℝ^P} #(B_α ∩ h_α⁻¹{y}) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{B_α} Jh_α dLⁿ. Since ψ_α : B_α → A_α is bijective and h_α = f∘ψ_α, #(B_α ∩ h_α⁻¹{y}) = #(A_α ∩ f⁻¹{y}) (SimonGMT's multiplicity is a tsum of 1 over the fibre, equal to encard by ENNReal.tsum_set_one). The injective weighted area formula for ψ_α on B_α (Simon Ch. 2 (4.13); SimonGMT Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum, each fibre of the injective ψ_α having at most one point) gives ∫_{A_α} w dHⁿ = ∫_{B_α} w(ψ_α(u)) Jψ_α(u) du for Hⁿ⌞A_α-measurable w ≥ 0. With w = J^M_f (Step 4) and (c'):
 ∫_{A_α} J^M_f dHⁿ = ∫_{B_α} J^M_f(ψ_α u) Jψ_α(u) du = ∫_{B_α} Jh_α du = ∫_{ℝ^P} #(A_α ∩ f⁻¹{y}) dHⁿ(y).

6. Summation, (2.4) (Simon lines 393-396). Countable additivity of the integral over the disjoint measurable A_α (A_∞ null) and monotone convergence (Mathlib lintegral_tsum; each y ↦ #(A_α ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = #(B_α ∩ h_α⁻¹{y}) is Hⁿ-a.e. measurable by SimonGMT aemeasurable_weightedAreaFiberSum_lipschitzOn, i.e. Simon Ch. 2, 1.8(ii)) give
 ∫_A J^M_f dHⁿ = Σ_α ∫ #(A_α ∩ f⁻¹{y}) dHⁿ(y) = ∫ Σ_α #(A_α ∩ f⁻¹{y}) dHⁿ(y) = ∫ #((A ∖ A_∞) ∩ f⁻¹{y}) dHⁿ(y),
 using additivity of encard over the disjoint union. Finally #(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = #((A ∖ A_∞) ∩ f⁻¹{y}) unless y ∈ f(A_∞), and Hⁿ(f(A_∞)) = 0 because A_∞ ⊆ U is Hⁿ-null and f is locally Lipschitz on U (Simon line 395, “the (easily checked) fact”: cover U by countably many balls on which f is Lipschitz). So the two integrands agree Hⁿ-a.e., proving (b).

7. Formula (2.5) (Simon lines 397-401). Let h : ℝ^N → [0, ∞] be Hⁿ⌞M-measurable. Take A := M in Step 3 (M_α, B_α). For each α, w_α(u) := h(ψ_α(u)) is Lⁿ⌞B_α-measurable (ψ_α bi-Lipschitz). The weighted fibre-sum area formula for h_α on B_α (Simon Ch. 2 (3.5); SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum) and Steps 2, 5 give
 ∫_{ℝ^P} Σ_{u∈B_α∩h_α⁻¹{y}} h(ψ_α u) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{B_α} Jh_α(u) h(ψ_α u) du = ∫_{B_α} h(ψ_α u) J^M_f(ψ_α u) Jψ_α(u) du = ∫_{M_α} h·J^M_f dHⁿ,
 and Σ_{u∈B_α∩h_α⁻¹{y}} h(ψ_α u) = Σ_{x∈M_α∩f⁻¹{y}} h(x); each of these fibre sums is an Hⁿ-a.e. measurable function of y (SimonGMT aemeasurable_weightedAreaFiberSum_lipschitzOn), as needed for monotone convergence. Summing over α (monotone convergence; [0,∞]-valued sums over the disjoint pieces M_α ∩ f⁻¹{y} add up to the sum over (M ∖ M_∞) ∩ f⁻¹{y}), and discarding M_∞ as in Step 6 (both sides: M_∞ is Hⁿ-null and Hⁿ(f(M_∞)) = 0), we get ∫_M h·J^M_f dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝ^P} Σ_{x∈M∩f⁻¹{y}} h(x) dHⁿ(y), which is (c). ∎
proof_key_steps: Lemma 1.2 (sibling) + Lindelöf: countably many good chart balls (ψ_α, D_α), ψ_α bi-Lipschitz, f∘ψ_α Lipschitz, covering M up to an Hⁿ-null set.
Sibling chart lemma: at a.e. parameter, T_xM = range Dψ_α(u) (uniqueness), d^Mf_x∘Dψ_α(u) = D(f∘ψ_α)(u) (uniqueness of line derivatives); this gives (a).
Jacobian chain rule (Simon (4.11), Mathlib normDet_comp): J(f∘ψ_α) = J^M_f∘ψ_α · Jψ_α; measurability of J^M_f.
Disjoint decomposition of A into pieces A_α = ψ_α(B_α) plus an Hⁿ-null set.
On each piece: SimonGMT Lipschitz area formula for f∘ψ_α and injective weighted area formula for ψ_α.
Sum over α (monotone convergence, additivity of encard); the null piece has Hⁿ-null image; weighted version gives (c).
