subproblem.title: Co-area formula (2.8)-(2.9) and rectifiability of slices (Remark 2.10(2))
subproblem.statement: Let m, k, ℓ ∈ ℕ with k > 0, n := m + k, M ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} countably n-rectifiable, U ⊇ M open and f : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝᵐ locally Lipschitz on U. (CoareaFormula) If moreover M is Hⁿ-measurable and θ is a positive locally integrable weight on M, then with J*^M_f(x) := coareaJacobian (approxTangentPlane n M θ x) f x: (a) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there are P and L with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P and HasTangentialDifferentialAt P f x L; (b) ∫_A J*^M_f dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝᵐ} Hᵏ(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) dLᵐ(y) and (c) ∫_A g·J*^M_f dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝᵐ} ∫_{A ∩ f⁻¹{y}} g dHᵏ dLᵐ(y) for every Hⁿ-measurable A ⊆ M and every Hⁿ⌞A-measurable g : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → [0, ∞]. (SlicesAreRectifiable) If M is Hⁿ-measurable, then M ∩ f⁻¹{y} is countably k-rectifiable for Lᵐ-a.e. y ∈ ℝᵐ.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 3, (2.7)-(2.9) and Remark 2.10(2), chapter-03.txt lines 412-442 (printed p. 77): “This follows from the C¹ case (see §6 of Ch. 2) by using the decomposition M = ∪M_j of Remark 1.3 and the C¹ Approximation Theorem 1.5 of Ch. 2 in a similar manner to the procedure used for the discussion of the area formula above” (lines 426-428), and 2.10(2) “follows directly from the decomposition … together with the C¹ Sard-type Theorem 6.4 of Ch. 2 and the C¹ Approximation Theorem 1.5” (lines 440-442). The C¹ case is Ch. 2, (6.3), (6.4), (6.6) (chapter-02.txt lines 1410-1510, printed pp. 65-67), whose proof Simon does not give (“See [Har79] or [Fed69] for the details”, p. 66). Departures, stated explicitly: (i) we supply a proof of the needed C¹ coarea formula, in parameter form (Lemma L3 below, following the standard proof of [Fed69, 3.2.12, 3.2.22] / Evans-Gariepy, Thm 3.11: implicit function theorem + Fubini on the regular set, a covering argument on the critical set); (ii) the null parts of the decomposition, which Simon passes over, are handled by Eilenberg's inequality (sibling eilenberg_inequality = Simon Ch. 2, 1.9); (iii) erratum in (2.9) (README): the domains are A on both sides (printed ∫_A on the left and f⁻¹(y) ∩ M on the right).

Notation. n = m + k with k ≥ 1; N := n + ℓ; ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d); Hˢ = μHE[s] (on ℝ^N or ℝⁿ as indicated); Lᵈ = volume on ℝ^d. For x ∈ M: T_xM := approxTangentPlane n M θ x, d^Mf_x := tangentialDifferential T_xM f x, J*^M_f(x) := coareaJacobian T_xM f x = normDet((d^Mf_x)*). For a linear L, normDet is Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet (|det| in orthonormal bases when source and range dimensions agree; normDet_comp: normDet(g∘f) = normDet(g.domRestrict(range f))·normDet(f)). For C¹ ψ, Jψ(u) := normDet(Dψ(u)).

Statement. CoareaFormula ∧ SlicesAreRectifiable (see the Lean statement): for m, k, ℓ with k > 0, M ⊆ ℝ^N countably (m+k)-rectifiable, U ⊇ M open, f : ℝ^N → ℝᵐ locally Lipschitz on U: (CO) if moreover M is H^{m+k}-measurable and θ is a positive locally integrable weight on M, then (a) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there are P, L with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P and HasTangentialDifferentialAt P f x L; (b) ∫_A J*^M_f dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝᵐ} Hᵏ(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) dLᵐ(y) and (c) ∫_A g·J*^M_f dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝᵐ}∫_{A∩f⁻¹{y}} g dHᵏ dLᵐ(y) for Hⁿ-measurable A ⊆ M and Hⁿ⌞A-measurable g ≥ 0; (SL) if M is Hⁿ-measurable (not used), then M ∩ f⁻¹{y} is countably k-rectifiable for Lᵐ-a.e. y.

Part 0. Preliminaries.

0.1 Case m = 0. Then ℝᵐ = ℝ⁰ = {0}, L⁰ is the unit point mass, f⁻¹{0} = ℝ^N and n = k. Every linear map into ℝ⁰ is 0, its adjoint is the zero map ℝ⁰ → T_xM, whose normDet is 1 (empty determinant), so J*^M_f ≡ 1; (b), (c) read ∫_A g dHⁿ = ∫_A g dHⁿ; (SL) says M itself is countably n-rectifiable (hypothesis); (a) is proved in 1.2 below (it does not use m ≥ 1). Assume m ≥ 1 in Lemmas L1-L3.

0.2 Null sets have null slices (from the sibling eilenberg_inequality, Simon Ch. 2, 1.9). (i) If Z ⊆ U with Hⁿ(Z) = 0, then Hᵏ(Z ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y. Proof: U is covered by countably many open balls B_b on which f is Lipschitz; extend f|B_b to a Lipschitz f_b : ℝ^N → ℝᵐ (Simon Ch. 2, 1.2, coordinatewise). Eilenberg's inequality for Z ∩ B_b, f_b, gives a Borel g_b ≥ Hᵏ(Z ∩ B_b ∩ f_b⁻¹{y}) with ∫ g_b ≤ C·Lip(f_b)ᵐ·Hⁿ(Z ∩ B_b) = 0, so g_b = 0 a.e.; as f = f_b on B_b, Hᵏ(Z ∩ B_b ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = 0 for a.e. y; take the countable union. (ii) The same holds in parameter space: if O ⊆ ℝⁿ is open, G : O → ℝᵐ is locally Lipschitz and Z ⊆ O is Lⁿ-null then Hᵏ(Z ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = 0 for a.e. y (same proof with N := n; Lⁿ(Z) = 0 gives μHE[m+k](Z) = 0 on ℝ^{m+k} by EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).

Part L. The C¹ case (Simon Ch. 2, (6.3)-(6.6), in parameter form).

L1 (critical slices; Simon's consequence of 6.3 stated before 6.4: “Hᵏ(C ∩ f⁻¹(y)) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y”). Let O ⊆ ℝⁿ be open, G : O → ℝᵐ C¹, C := {u ∈ O : rank DG(u) < m} (relatively closed in O, rank being lower semicontinuous). Then Hᵏ(C ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y.
Proof. O is a countable union of closed cubes Q₀ ⊆ O; fix one, of side a, and Λ := max_{Q₀}‖DG‖. For j ≥ 1 choose an integer M_j ≥ j such that, with s_j := a/M_j, ‖DG(u) − DG(u')‖ ≤ 1/j for u, u' ∈ Q₀, |u − u'| ≤ √n s_j (uniform continuity). Divide Q₀ into M_jⁿ closed subcubes Q of side s_j. If Q ∩ C ≠ ∅ pick u_Q ∈ Q ∩ C; the range of DG(u_Q) lies in a hyperplane H_Q of ℝᵐ. By the mean value inequality, for u ∈ Q, G(u) = G(u_Q) + DG(u_Q)(u − u_Q) + e with |e| ≤ √n s_j/j and |DG(u_Q)(u − u_Q)| ≤ Λ√n s_j; hence G(Q) lies in a set {v : |p_{H_Q}(v − G(u_Q))| ≤ (Λ + 1)√n s_j, |p_{H_Q^⊥}(v − G(u_Q))| ≤ √n s_j/j}, so Lᵐ(G(Q)) ≤ C₂ s_jᵐ/j with C₂ := 2ω_{m−1}((Λ + 1)√n)^{m−1}√n. Let g_j(y) := Σ_{Q∩C≠∅} c_k(√n s_j)^k 1_{G(Q∩C)}(y) (G(Q ∩ C) is compact; c_k as in the definition of H^k_δ, cf. eilenberg_inequality). Since C ∩ Q₀ ∩ G⁻¹{y} is covered by the subcubes Q (diameter √n s_j) with y ∈ G(Q ∩ C), H^k_{√n s_j}(C ∩ Q₀ ∩ G⁻¹{y}) ≤ g_j(y), while ∫ g_j dLᵐ ≤ M_jⁿ c_k n^{k/2} s_j^k C₂ s_jᵐ/j = c_k n^{k/2} C₂ aⁿ/j → 0. With g := liminf g_j (Borel), Hᵏ(C ∩ Q₀ ∩ G⁻¹{y}) ≤ g(y) and ∫ g ≤ liminf ∫ g_j = 0 (Fatou), so g = 0 a.e. ∎

Convention for L2-L3: fix a linear isometry e : ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ → ℝⁿ (Euclidean product, e.g. via finSumFinEquiv) and identify ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ with ℝⁿ through e; e maps Lᵐ ⊗ Lᵏ to Lⁿ, and |det DΦ(u)| denotes the absolute Jacobian determinant of the map ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, u ↦ e(Φ(u)) (this is what LA computes in orthonormal bases).

L2 (regular points; Simon p. 66: “the implicit function theorem implies that … f⁻¹(y) ∖ C … is a k-dimensional C¹ submanifold”). Let O, G be as in L1 and u₀ ∈ O ∖ C. Let K₀ := ker DG(u₀) (dimension k) and π := ι∘p_{K₀} : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ with ι : K₀ → ℝᵏ a linear isometry. Then Φ := (G, π) : O → ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ (≅ ℝⁿ) has invertible DΦ(u₀) (if DG(u₀)v = 0 and πv = 0 then v ∈ K₀ and v = 0). By the inverse function theorem there is an open O' ∋ u₀, O' ⊆ O ∖ C, such that Φ|O' is a C¹ diffeomorphism onto an open Ω with DΦ(u) invertible on O'. For y ∈ ℝᵐ put Ω_y := {z : (y, z) ∈ Ω} (open); then O' ∩ G⁻¹{y} = {Φ⁻¹(y, z) : z ∈ Ω_y}, and z ↦ Φ⁻¹(y, z) is C¹ and injective on Ω_y with derivative E_u := DΦ(u)⁻¹|_{{0}×ℝᵏ} (u = Φ⁻¹(y, z)), an isomorphism of ℝᵏ onto ker DG(u) (DG(u)E_u = 0, πE_u = id).

LA (linear algebra). Let A : ℝⁿ → T be a linear isomorphism onto an n-dimensional inner product space T, Γ : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ surjective, K := ker Γ, π : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ with π|K invertible, E := (π|K)⁻¹ : ℝᵏ → K, and Λ := Γ∘A⁻¹ : T → ℝᵐ. Then normDet(A∘E)·|det(Γ, π)| = normDet(Λ*)·normDet(A).
Proof. Use orthonormal bases adapted to ℝⁿ = K^⊥ ⊕ K, T = A(K) ⊕ A(K)^⊥, ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ. (Γ, π) is block lower triangular ((Γ, π)|K = (0, π|K)), so |det(Γ, π)| = |det(Γ|K^⊥)|·|det(π|K)| = |det(Γ|K^⊥)|/|det E|. By normDet_comp, normDet(A∘E) = normDet(A|K)·|det E| (range E = K). A is block upper triangular w.r.t. (K ⊕ K^⊥) → (A(K) ⊕ A(K)^⊥) with diagonal blocks A|K and A₂₂ := p_{A(K)^⊥}∘A|K^⊥, so normDet(A) = normDet(A|K)·|det A₂₂|. Since ker Λ = A(K), Γ|K^⊥ = Λ∘A|K^⊥ = Λ|_{A(K)^⊥}∘A₂₂, so |det(Γ|K^⊥)| = |det(Λ|_{A(K)^⊥})|·|det A₂₂|, and |det(Λ|_{A(K)^⊥})| = normDet(Λ*) (Λ* is an isomorphism of ℝᵐ onto (ker Λ)^⊥ = A(K)^⊥, adjoint to Λ|_{A(K)^⊥}). Multiplying: normDet(A∘E)|det(Γ, π)| = normDet(A|K)·normDet(Λ*)·|det A₂₂| = normDet(Λ*)·normDet(A). ∎

L3 (C¹ coarea formula in parameter form = Simon Ch. 2, (6.3), (6.6) for the submanifold ψ(D) and g = G∘ψ⁻¹, transported by the area formula). Let D ⊆ ℝⁿ be open, ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N C¹ on a neighbourhood of D̄, injective and bi-Lipschitz on D with Dψ(u) injective, and G : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ C¹. For u ∈ D let T_u := range Dψ(u), Λ_u := DG(u)∘(Dψ(u))⁻¹ : T_u → ℝᵐ and J*(u) := normDet(Λ_u*). Then for every Lⁿ-measurable B ⊆ D and Borel φ : ℝ^N → [0, ∞]: the function y ↦ ∫_{ψ(B∩G⁻¹{y})} φ dHᵏ is Lᵐ-a.e. measurable and
 ∫_B φ(ψ(u)) J*(u) Jψ(u) du = ∫_{ℝᵐ} ∫_{ψ(B∩G⁻¹{y})} φ dHᵏ dLᵐ(y).
Proof. (a) Critical part, B ⊆ C := {u ∈ D : rank DG(u) < m}: Λ_u is not surjective, so Λ_u* is not injective and J*(u) = 0; the left side is 0. By L1, Hᵏ(C ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = 0 for a.e. y, and ψ is Lipschitz on D, so Hᵏ(ψ(B ∩ G⁻¹{y})) = 0 and the right integrand vanishes a.e. (b) B ⊆ O' for O', Φ, Ω, E_u as in L2: put B' := Φ(B) (Lebesgue measurable) and B'_y := {z : (y, z) ∈ B'}. Write B' = B'' ∪ Z'' with B'' Borel and Lⁿ(Z'') = 0; by Tonelli Lᵏ((Z'')_y) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y, so for those y the section B'_y is Lᵏ-measurable. For each such y, ψ(B ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = χ_y(B'_y) with χ_y(z) := ψ(Φ⁻¹(y, z)), a C¹ injective immersion of Ω_y with Dχ_y(z) = Dψ(u)E_u. By the injective area formula on the k-dimensional parameter domain (Simon Ch. 2, (3.2), (4.13); SimonGMT injective/weighted area formulas for Lipschitz maps, applied on countably many compact pieces of Ω_y where χ_y is Lipschitz), ∫_{χ_y(B'_y)} φ dHᵏ = ∫_{B'_y} φ(χ_y(z)) normDet(Dψ(u)E_u) dz. By Tonelli on ℝᵐ × ℝᵏ (which also gives the a.e.-measurability in y) and the change of variables formula for the C¹ diffeomorphism Φ:
 ∫_{ℝᵐ}∫_{ψ(B∩G⁻¹{y})} φ dHᵏ dy = ∫_{B'} φ(ψ(Φ⁻¹(y, z))) normDet(Dψ(u)E_u)|_{u=Φ⁻¹(y,z)} d(y, z) = ∫_B φ(ψ(u)) normDet(Dψ(u)E_u)|det DΦ(u)| du,
 and LA (with A = Dψ(u), Γ = DG(u)) turns the integrand into φ(ψ(u)) J*(u) Jψ(u). (c) General B: D ∖ C is covered by countably many O'_t as in L2 (Lindelöf); B = (B ∩ C) ⊔ ⨆_t B_t with B_t := (B ∩ O'_t) ∖ ⋃_{t'<t} O'_{t'}. The left side is countably additive in B. On the right, for each y the sets ψ(B_t ∩ G⁻¹{y}) are pairwise disjoint (ψ injective); writing B_t = B_t^b ∪ Z_t with B_t^b Borel and Lⁿ(Z_t) = 0, the sets ψ(B_t^b ∩ G⁻¹{y}) are Borel (ψ restricted to each compact subset of D is a homeomorphism onto its image, and D is σ-compact), and Hᵏ(ψ(Z_t ∩ G⁻¹{y})) = 0 for a.e. y by 0.2(ii) and the Lipschitz bound for ψ. Hence for a.e. y, ∫ over ψ(B ∩ G⁻¹{y}) is the sum of the integrals over the pieces, and (a), (b) and monotone convergence give the formula. ∎

Part 1. The coarea formula for M (CO).

1.1 Good chart balls. Exactly as in the area formula (Simon Remark 1.3 and Lemma 1.2 via the sibling submanifold_cover; Lindelöf): countably many (ψ_α, D_α), α ∈ ℕ, D_α an open ball with closure in the chart domain, ψ_α C¹ near D̄_α, injective and bi-Lipschitz on D_α with injective derivative, ψ_α(D̄_α) ⊆ B_{s_α}(x_α) ⊆ U where f is Lipschitz on B_{s_α}(x_α), and M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_α ψ_α(D_α), Hⁿ(N₀) = 0 (choose the balls so that their interiors already cover V ∩ ψ⁻¹(U) for each chart V). h_α := f∘ψ_α is Lipschitz on D_α.

1.2 Pointwise identification and (a). Apply the sibling chart_tangent_differential to (M, U, θ, f) and the chart of α: there is an Lⁿ-null Z_α ⊆ D_α such that for u ∈ D_α ∖ Z_α with x := ψ_α(u) ∈ M: HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T_u (T_u := range Dψ_α(u)), h_α is differentiable at u, and HasLineDerivAt ℝ f (Dh_α(u)w) x (Dψ_α(u)w) for all w. As in the area formula (uniqueness of weighted tangent planes, SimonGMT HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, θ(x) > 0; uniqueness of line derivatives) T_xM = T_u and d^Mf_x = L_x where L_x∘Dψ_α(u) = Dh_α(u). Hence J*^M_f(x) = normDet(L_x*). Conclusion (a) holds off the Hⁿ-null set N₀ ∪ ⋃_α ψ_α(Z_α) with P := T_u, L := L_x.

1.3 C¹ approximation (Simon line 427). Extend h_α|D̄_α to a Lipschitz h̃_α : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ (Simon Ch. 2, 1.2, coordinatewise). By the sibling c1_approximation, for i ≥ 1 there is a C¹ G_{α,i} : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ with Lⁿ({h̃_α ≠ G_{α,i}} ∪ {Dh̃_α ≠ DG_{α,i}}) < 1/i. Let E_{α,i} := {u ∈ D_α ∖ Z_α : h̃_α differentiable at u, h̃_α(u) = G_{α,i}(u), Dh̃_α(u) = DG_{α,i}(u)}. Then Lⁿ(D_α ∖ ⋃ᵢ E_{α,i}) = 0, and for u ∈ E_{α,i}: h_α(u) = G_{α,i}(u), Dh_α(u) = DG_{α,i}(u) (u is interior to D_α), so L_x = DG_{α,i}(u)∘(Dψ_α(u))⁻¹ = Λ_u for G := G_{α,i}, ψ := ψ_α, and J*^M_f(ψ_α(u)) = J*(u) in the notation of L3.

1.4 Decomposition. Let A ⊆ M be Hⁿ-measurable and g ≥ 0 Hⁿ⌞A-measurable; choose Borel g' with g = g' Hⁿ⌞A-a.e. Put A_α := (A ∩ ψ_α(D_α)) ∖ ⋃_{β<α} ψ_β(D_β), B_α := D_α ∩ ψ_α⁻¹(A_α) (Lⁿ-measurable), B_{α,i} := (B_α ∩ E_{α,i}) ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} E_{α,i'}, A_{α,i} := ψ_α(B_{α,i}). Then A = A_null ⊔ ⨆_{α,i} A_{α,i} with A_null ⊆ (A ∩ N₀) ∪ ⋃_α ψ_α(D_α ∖ ⋃_i E_{α,i}) Hⁿ-null, the A_{α,i} pairwise disjoint and Hⁿ-measurable, and A_{α,i} ∩ f⁻¹{y} = ψ_α(B_{α,i} ∩ G_{α,i}⁻¹{y}) (for u ∈ B_{α,i}, f(ψ_α(u)) = h_α(u) = G_{α,i}(u)).

1.5 One piece. L3 with D := D_α, ψ := ψ_α, G := G_{α,i}, B := B_{α,i}, φ := g' gives ∫_{B_{α,i}} g'(ψ_α u) J*(u) Jψ_α(u) du = ∫_{ℝᵐ}∫_{A_{α,i}∩f⁻¹{y}} g' dHᵏ dy (inner function a.e. measurable). By 1.3 and the injective weighted area formula for ψ_α on B_{α,i} (as in the area formula), the left side equals ∫_{A_{α,i}} g'·J*^M_f dHⁿ (in particular J*^M_f is Hⁿ⌞A-measurable, being a.e. equal on each A_{α,i} to the transport of the measurable J* by the bi-Lipschitz ψ_α).

1.6 Summation. Summing over (α, i) (monotone convergence on both sides; A_null contributes 0 on the left):
 ∫_A g'·J*^M_f dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝᵐ} Σ_{α,i} ∫_{A_{α,i}∩f⁻¹{y}} g' dHᵏ dy.
 For Lᵐ-a.e. y: Hᵏ(A_null ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = 0 (0.2(i)); each A_{α,i} ∩ f⁻¹{y} is the union of a Borel set and an Hᵏ-null set (write B_{α,i} = Borel ∪ Lⁿ-null set Z' and use 0.2(ii) for Z' and G_{α,i}, then the Lipschitz bound for ψ_α); so Σ_{α,i}∫_{A_{α,i}∩f⁻¹{y}} g' dHᵏ = ∫_{A∩f⁻¹{y}} g' dHᵏ. Finally {g ≠ g'} ∩ A is Hⁿ-null, so it does not change the left side and, by 0.2(i), its slices are Hᵏ-null for a.e. y, so g' may be replaced by g on the right. This proves (c) (Simon (2.9) with the corrected domain A), and (b) (Simon (2.8)) is the case g ≡ 1. Together with 1.2 this proves CoareaFormula.

Part 2. Slices (SL) (Simon Remark 2.10(2), lines 439-442).

2.1 With (ψ_α, D_α), h̃_α, G_{α,i} as in 1.1, 1.3 (Z_α is not needed here; replace E_{α,i} by E'_{α,i} := D_α ∩ {h̃_α = G_{α,i}}), Lⁿ(D_α ∖ ⋃_i E'_{α,i}) = 0, and M ⊆ M_null ∪ ⋃_{α,i} ψ_α(E'_{α,i}) with M_null := (M ∩ N₀) ∪ ⋃_α ψ_α(D_α ∖ ⋃_i E'_{α,i}) Hⁿ-null. For every y, M ∩ f⁻¹{y} ⊆ (M_null ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ∪ ⋃_{α,i} ψ_α(E'_{α,i} ∩ G_{α,i}⁻¹{y}). No measurability of M is used.

2.2 Fix (α, i), G := G_{α,i}, C := {u ∈ D_α : rank DG(u) < m}. (R) For every y, (D_α ∖ C) ∩ G⁻¹{y} is covered by countably many sets O'_t ∩ G⁻¹{y} = {Φ_t⁻¹(y, z) : z ∈ (Ω_t)_y} (L2), so ψ_α((D_α ∖ C) ∩ G⁻¹{y}) ⊆ ⋃_t ψ_α∘Φ_t⁻¹(y, ·)((Ω_t)_y), a countable union of images of open subsets of ℝᵏ under C¹ maps, each countably k-rectifiable (SimonGMT Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_image_contDiffOn_open, with dimension k); this is the regular part of Simon's C¹ Sard-type Theorem 6.4. (C) By L1, Hᵏ(C ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y, hence Hᵏ(ψ_α(C ∩ G⁻¹{y})) = 0 (ψ_α Lipschitz on D_α); this is the critical part of 6.4.

2.3 Conclusion. By 0.2(i), Hᵏ(M_null ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y. Let Y be the complement of the union of the countably many exceptional Lᵐ-null sets from 2.2(C) and 0.2(i). For y ∈ Y, M ∩ f⁻¹{y} is contained in the union of an Hᵏ-null set and countably many countably k-rectifiable sets, hence is countably k-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, countablyRectifiable_iUnion, CountablyRectifiable.mono). This proves SlicesAreRectifiable (for m = 0 it is the hypothesis, cf. 0.1). ∎
proof_key_steps: m = 0 is trivial (J* ≡ 1, L⁰ a point mass); null sets have Hᵏ-null slices for a.e. y by the sibling Eilenberg inequality.
L1: critical slices Hᵏ(C ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = 0 a.e. for C¹ G (covering argument).
L2/LA/L3: implicit function theorem, a linear-algebra identity for coarea factors, Fubini and change of variables give the C¹ coarea formula in parameter form (Simon Ch. 2 (6.3), (6.6)).
Good chart balls via Lemma 1.2 (sibling); identification of T_xM and d^Mf_x via the sibling chart lemma, giving (a).
C¹ approximation (sibling) of f∘ψ_α on pieces where values and derivatives agree, so J*^M_f∘ψ_α equals the parameter coarea factor.
Apply L3 on each piece, sum, and discard null pieces (Eilenberg) to get (b), (c).
Slices: regular parts of level sets are C¹ images of open subsets of ℝᵏ (countably k-rectifiable), critical parts and null parts have Hᵏ-null slices for a.e. y.

subproblem.title: Lemma 3.2, Lemma 3.3 and Theorem 3.8
subproblem.statement: (Lemma 3.2) If A ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} equals ⋃ⱼ Aⱼ with Hⁿ(Aⱼ) < ∞, then A = R ∪ P with R, P disjoint, R countably n-rectifiable and P purely n-unrectifiable, and if A is Hⁿ-measurable, R can be chosen Borel. (Lemma 3.3) If S ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} satisfies Hⁿ(coordinateProjection J (S)) = 0 for every J ⊆ Fin (n+ℓ) with #J = n, then S is purely n-unrectifiable. (Theorem 3.8) If A = ⋃ⱼ Aⱼ with Hⁿ(Aⱼ) < ∞ and every B ⊆ A with Hⁿ(B) > 0 satisfies ¬ForAlmostAllProjections (n+ℓ) n (fun p ↦ Hⁿ(p(B)) = 0), then A is countably n-rectifiable.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 3, Lemma 3.2 (chapter-03.txt lines 449-469, printed p. 78), Lemma 3.3 (lines 476-496, printed pp. 78-79) and Theorem 3.8 (lines 540-548, printed p. 80). Errata: Definition 3.1 (line 446) “if P contains” should read “if S contains” (as encoded by PurelyUnrectifiable); line 540 “by combining 3.2 and 3.7” should read “by combining 3.2 and 3.6” — Remark 3.7 is the converse direction (via Lemma 3.3), whereas the proof of 3.8 uses the null-projection theorem 3.6, supplied by the sibling besicovitch_federer.

Notation. N := n + ℓ, ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), Hⁿ = μHE[n], Lⁿ = volume = Hⁿ on ℝⁿ; coordinateProjection J is the orthogonal projection of ℝ^N onto span{e_j : j ∈ J}.

Statement. RectifiableDecomposition ∧ CoordinateProjectionCriterion ∧ RectifiabilityTheoremForSets.

Part 1: Lemma 3.2 (RectifiableDecomposition).
1. Let A = ⋃ⱼ Aⱼ with Hⁿ(Aⱼ) < ∞. SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.simon_lemma_3_2 (Chapter03/Rectifiable.lean), applied with the cover S := (Aⱼ)ⱼ (A ⊆ ⋃ⱼ Aⱼ, Hⁿ(Aⱼ) < ∞), gives exactly the first conclusion (A = R ∪ P, Disjoint R P, R countably n-rectifiable, P purely n-unrectifiable) and, if A is Hⁿ-null-measurable, a decomposition with additionally MeasurableSet R (and NullMeasurableSet P, which we drop). That Lean proof implements Simon's argument (lines 455-469): reduce to the measurable case via Borel hulls of the Aⱼ; maximize Hⁿ over Borel countably rectifiable subsets (σ-finiteness of Hⁿ⌞A) to get a Borel countably rectifiable R capturing, up to Hⁿ-null sets, every rectifiable subset of A; then A ∖ R is purely unrectifiable.

Part 2: Lemma 3.3 (CoordinateProjectionCriterion), Simon lines 482-496.
2. Case n = 0. For J = ∅, coordinateProjection ∅ is the zero map, so coordinateProjection ∅ '' S = {0} if S ≠ ∅, of H⁰-measure 1. The hypothesis therefore forces S = ∅, which is purely 0-unrectifiable. Assume n ≥ 1.
3. Linear algebra (Simon lines 482-489). If L ⊆ ℝ^N is an n-dimensional subspace, there is J ⊆ {1, …, N} with #J = n such that coordinateProjection J restricted to L is a linear isomorphism onto span{e_j : j ∈ J}. Proof: the coordinate functionals x ↦ x_j restricted to L span the dual space L* (a nonzero x ∈ L has some nonzero coordinate), which has dimension n, so n of them, indexed by some J, form a basis of L*; then x ↦ (x_j)_{j∈J} is injective on L, i.e. coordinateProjection J (x ↦ Σ_{j∈J} x_j e_j) is injective on L, and both spaces have dimension n. (This is SimonGMT Chapter03/CoordinateProjection.lean, exists_bijective_selectedCoordinateMap, which returns an injective j : Fin n → Fin N with selectedCoordinateMap L j bijective; take J := Finset.univ.image j, of cardinality n since j is injective. That file is not imported by the contract, but its short proof can be reproduced.)
4. Suppose S is not purely n-unrectifiable: there is R ⊆ S countably n-rectifiable with Hⁿ(R) > 0. By the sibling submanifold_cover (Lemma 1.2, “⇒”), R ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃ⱼ Nⱼ with Hⁿ(N₀) = 0 and IsC1Submanifold n Nⱼ; by countable subadditivity Hⁿ(R ∩ N) > 0 for N := Nⱼ, some j (Simon lines 490-491). N is a countable union of chart images ψ(V) (V ⊆ ℝⁿ open, ψ C¹ with injective derivative; Lindelöf), and V is a countable union of closed balls D on which ψ is bi-Lipschitz (choose D = B̄_r(u) with ‖Dψ − Dψ(u)‖ ≤ c/2 on D, c := min_{|v|=1}|Dψ(u)v|, and use the mean value inequality). So some chart and ball have Hⁿ(R ∩ ψ(D)) > 0. Let T' := D ∩ ψ⁻¹(R); then Lⁿ(T') > 0 (outer measure), since Hⁿ(R ∩ ψ(D)) = Hⁿ(ψ(T')) ≤ Lip(ψ|D)ⁿ Lⁿ(T'). There is u₀ ∈ T' with Lⁿ(T' ∩ B(u₀, ρ)) > 0 for every ρ > 0 (otherwise T' is covered by countably many Lⁿ-null balls; Simon line 492: “there must be some x ∈ S ∩ N with Hⁿ(S ∩ N ∩ B_ρ(x)) > 0 for all ρ > 0”).
5. Local diffeomorphism (Simon lines 493-496, via Ch. 2, Remark 4.4). Let L := range Dψ(u₀) (n-dimensional), J as in Step 3, and ι_J : ℝⁿ → span{e_j : j ∈ J} a linear isometry. Φ := ι_J⁻¹ ∘ coordinateProjection J ∘ ψ is C¹ near u₀ with DΦ(u₀) = ι_J⁻¹ ∘ coordinateProjection J ∘ Dψ(u₀), a linear isomorphism of ℝⁿ. By the mean value inequality (as in Step 4; the inverse function theorem is not needed) there are ρ > 0 and c > 0 with B(u₀, ρ) ⊆ V and |Φ(u) − Φ(u')| ≥ c|u − u'| for u, u' ∈ B(u₀, ρ). Hence Lⁿ(T' ∩ B(u₀, ρ)) ≤ c^{-n} Hⁿ(Φ(T' ∩ B(u₀, ρ))) (Φ⁻¹ is c⁻¹-Lipschitz on the image), and since ι_J is an isometry and ψ(T') ⊆ R ⊆ S:
 Hⁿ(coordinateProjection J '' S) ≥ Hⁿ(coordinateProjection J (ψ(T' ∩ B(u₀, ρ)))) = Hⁿ(Φ(T' ∩ B(u₀, ρ))) ≥ cⁿ Lⁿ(T' ∩ B(u₀, ρ)) > 0,
 contradicting the hypothesis (#J = n). Hence S is purely n-unrectifiable.

Part 3: Theorem 3.8 (RectifiabilityTheoremForSets), Simon lines 540-548 (with the erratum above).
6. Let A = ⋃ⱼ Aⱼ, Hⁿ(Aⱼ) < ∞, and assume every B ⊆ A with Hⁿ(B) > 0 satisfies ¬ForAlmostAllProjections (n+ℓ) n (fun p ↦ Hⁿ(p '' B) = 0). By Part 1, A = R ∪ P with R countably n-rectifiable and P purely n-unrectifiable. P ⊆ A and P = ⋃ⱼ (P ∩ Aⱼ) with Hⁿ(P ∩ Aⱼ) ≤ Hⁿ(Aⱼ) < ∞, so the sibling besicovitch_federer (Theorem 3.6) gives ForAlmostAllProjections (n+ℓ) n (fun p ↦ Hⁿ(p '' P) = 0). If Hⁿ(P) > 0, the hypothesis applied to B := P contradicts this; hence Hⁿ(P) = 0. Then P is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero) and A = R ∪ P is countably n-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_iUnion with the two-member family, or directly: if R ⊆ R₀ ∪ ⋃ⱼ Fⱼ(ℝⁿ) then A ⊆ (R₀ ∪ P) ∪ ⋃ⱼ Fⱼ(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(R₀ ∪ P) = 0). ∎
proof_key_steps: 3.2: SimonGMT simon_lemma_3_2 with the cover (Aⱼ).
3.3, n = 0: the hypothesis forces S = ∅.
3.3 linear algebra: every n-plane is mapped isomorphically by some coordinate projection.

3.3: a rectifiable subset of positive measure meets some C¹ chart (Lemma 1.2 sibling) in a set with a parameter density point u₀; near u₀ the coordinate projection composed with the chart is bi-Lipschitz, so the projection of S has positive measure.
3.8: decompose A = R ∪ P by 3.2; Besicovitch-Federer (sibling) gives null projections of P a.e., so Hⁿ(P) = 0 by hypothesis and A is countably rectifiable.

subproblem.title: Theorems 1.6 and 1.9: rectifiability iff approximate tangent spaces exist a.e. (unweighted and weighted)
subproblem.statement: (Theorem 1.6) For all n, ℓ and every Hⁿ-measurable M ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K: M is countably n-rectifiable iff for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is a subspace P with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x P (Simon Definition 1.4: finrank P = n and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_P f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0 for all f ∈ C_c). (Theorem 1.9) For all n, ℓ, every Hⁿ-measurable M ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} and every positive locally integrable weight θ on M: M is countably n-rectifiable iff for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is P with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P (Definition 1.7: finrank P = n and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dHⁿ(y) → θ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ for all f ∈ C_c).
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 3, Theorem 1.6 (chapter-03.txt lines 109-111; proof “⇒” lines 113-143, proof “⇐” lines 145-274) and Theorem 1.9 (lines 316-323, derived from Remark 1.8(1), lines 298-306, and Theorem 1.6). The two analytic cores of Simon's proofs are supplied by siblings: the “⇒” argument (the density argument proving Remark 1.5(2), localized to C¹ charts and with multiplicity θ as in Remark 1.8(1)) is chart_tangent_differential, and the “⇐” argument (Lipschitz-graph construction, lines 145-274, which only uses properties (5), (6) of the measure) is rectifiable_of_tangent_measure, applied to μ = Hⁿ⌞M for 1.6 and to μ = θHⁿ⌞M for 1.9. Departure: Simon derives 1.9 from 1.6 via Lusin's theorem (Remark 1.8(1)); since both siblings already allow a multiplicity, we prove 1.9 directly in the same way as 1.6, which avoids the “straightforward check” of Remark 1.8(1).

Notation. N = n + ℓ, ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), Hⁿ = μHE[n], η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x) (blowUpMap). (F1) For x ∈ ℝ^N, r > 0, A ⊆ ℝ^N, ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} g dHⁿ = r^{-n}∫_A g∘η_{x,r} dHⁿ for every Borel g ≥ 0 and every g with g∘η_{x,r} ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞A): η_{x,r} is a similarity of ratio r⁻¹, so Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(S)) = r^{-n}Hⁿ(S) for all S (scaling and translation invariance of Hausdorff measure), i.e. (η_{x,r})_#(Hⁿ⌞A) = rⁿHⁿ⌞η_{x,r}(A). (F2) Locally Lipschitz maps on open subsets of ℝⁿ send Lⁿ-null sets to Hⁿ-null sets (cover the open set by countably many closed balls on which the map is Lipschitz; SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn).

Statement. ApproximateTangentCharacterization ∧ WeightedApproximateTangentCharacterization, i.e. for M ⊆ ℝ^N Hⁿ-measurable: (1.6) if Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for all compact K, then M is countably n-rectifiable iff for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M some P satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x P; (1.9) if θ is a positive locally integrable weight on M (IsPositiveLocallyIntegrableWeight n M θ), then M is countably n-rectifiable iff for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M some P satisfies HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P.

Proof.

1. Chart cover of a countably rectifiable set. Let M be countably n-rectifiable. By the sibling submanifold_cover (Lemma 1.2, “⇒”), M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_j N_j with Hⁿ(N₀) = 0 and IsC1Submanifold n N_j. For y ∈ N_j choose a chart (V_y, W_y, ψ_y) as in the definition (V_y ⊆ ℝⁿ open, ψ_y C¹ on V_y with injective derivative, ψ_y(V_y) = W_y ∩ N_j, y ∈ W_y). The open sets W_y cover N_j and ℝ^N is second countable, so countably many of them cover N_j; hence N_j = ⋃ᵢ ψ_{j,i}(V_{j,i}) for countably many charts (V_{j,i}, ψ_{j,i}).

2. A general “⇒” lemma. Let M be Hⁿ-measurable and countably n-rectifiable and θ a positive locally integrable weight on M. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is P with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P. Proof: apply the sibling chart_tangent_differential to each chart (V_{j,i}, ψ_{j,i}) of Step 1, with p := 0, f := 0, U := ℝ^N (f is Lipschitz, M ⊆ U). It yields Lⁿ-null sets Z_{j,i} ⊆ V_{j,i} such that for u ∈ V_{j,i} ∖ Z_{j,i} with ψ_{j,i}(u) ∈ M, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ (ψ_{j,i} u) (range Dψ_{j,i}(u)). The set Z := (M ∩ N₀) ∪ ⋃_{j,i} ψ_{j,i}(Z_{j,i}) is Hⁿ-null by (F2). If x ∈ M ∖ Z then x ∉ N₀, so x = ψ_{j,i}(u) for some j, i, u ∈ V_{j,i}, and u ∉ Z_{j,i} (otherwise x ∈ Z); hence P := range Dψ_{j,i}(u) works.

3. Theorem 1.6 “⇒” (Simon lines 113-143). Assume M countably n-rectifiable, Hⁿ-measurable, Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K. The constant θ ≡ 1 is a positive locally integrable weight on M: positive, measurable, and IntegrableOn 1 (M ∩ K) Hⁿ because Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞. By Step 2, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is P with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M 1 x P, which is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x P after rewriting f(y)·1 = f(y) and 1·∫_P f = ∫_P f (mul_one, one_mul).

4. Theorem 1.9 “⇒”. Immediate from Step 2 with the given θ.

5. From weighted tangent planes to tangent measures. Let θ be a positive locally integrable weight on the Hⁿ-measurable M, choose a Borel θ' ≥ 0 with θ' = θ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e., and let μ := (μHE[n].restrict M).withDensity (ENNReal.ofReal ∘ θ'), i.e. μ(A) = ∫_{A∩M} θ' dHⁿ, so that ∫ g dμ = ∫_M g θ' dHⁿ (Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul). Then μ(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K. If x ∈ M, θ(x) = θ'(x), and HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P, then for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) and r > 0, by (F1) applied to g(y) := f(y)θ'(x + ry), whose composite g∘η_{x,r}(z) = f(η_{x,r}(z))θ'(z) is integrable on M (bounded by ‖f‖_∞θ' with compact support):
 (rⁿ)⁻¹∫ f(η_{x,r}(y)) dμ(y) = r^{-n}∫_M f(η_{x,r}(z)) θ'(z) dHⁿ(z) = ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y) θ'(x + ry) dHⁿ(y),
 which equals ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dHⁿ(y) (the integrands differ only on the Hⁿ-null image of {θ ≠ θ'} ∩ M) and tends to θ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ. So HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x P (θ x), with θ(x) > 0 because x ∈ M. A property holding for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M holds μ-a.e. (μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, and M is null-measurable, so “Hⁿ-a.e. x, x ∈ M → …” is “Hⁿ⌞M-a.e.”). Finally, if R is Borel with μ(ℝ^N ∖ R) = 0, then ∫_{M∖R} θ dHⁿ = 0 and θ > 0 on M give Hⁿ(M ∖ R) = 0.

6. Theorems 1.6 “⇐” and 1.9 “⇐” (Simon lines 145-274; 316-323). Assume the tangent condition holds for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, with weight θ (for 1.6 take θ ≡ 1, which is admissible by Step 3, and note that HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x P is HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M 1 x P). By Step 5, μ satisfies the hypotheses of the sibling rectifiable_of_tangent_measure (finite on compacts; μ-a.e. x has an approximate tangent plane with positive multiplicity θ(x)). Hence there is a Borel countably n-rectifiable R with μ(ℝ^N ∖ R) = 0, and Step 5 gives Hⁿ(M ∖ R) = 0. Write R ⊆ R₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ) as in Definition 1.1; then M ⊆ ((M ∖ R) ∪ R₀) ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ((M ∖ R) ∪ R₀) = 0, so M is countably n-rectifiable. ∎
proof_key_steps: Lemma 1.2 (sibling) + Lindelöf: a countably rectifiable M is covered, up to an Hⁿ-null set, by countably many C¹ chart images.
'⇒' (both theorems): apply the sibling chart lemma (f = 0) in every chart; chart images of Lⁿ-null sets are Hⁿ-null; θ ≡ 1 gives Def. 1.4.
'⇐': the weighted tangent condition makes μ := θHⁿ⌞M (θ ≡ 1 for 1.6) a locally finite measure with approximate tangent planes of multiplicity θ(x) > 0, via the scaling identity for η_{x,r}.
The sibling measure lemma gives a Borel countably rectifiable R with μ(ℝ^N ∖ R) = 0, hence Hⁿ(M ∖ R) = 0 as θ > 0 on M.
M ⊆ (M ∖ R) ∪ R is countably n-rectifiable.

subproblem.title: Theorem 4.3 (De Giorgi): structure of the reduced boundary
subproblem.statement: For n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} open and E Lebesgue null-measurable with locally finite perimeter in U: a Gauss-Green pair (μ, ν) for (U, E) exists, and for every Gauss-Green pair (μ, ν), with ∂*E := reducedBoundary U μ ν (points of U where the open-ball averages μ(B_ρ(x))⁻¹∫_{B_ρ(x)}ν dμ converge as ρ ↓ 0 to a unit vector) and ν_E := reducedNormal μ ν (that limit): ∂*E is countably n-rectifiable; μ = Hⁿ⌞∂*E as measures on ℝ^{n+1}; for every x ∈ ∂*E, μ has approximate tangent plane (span{ν_E(x)})^⊥ at x with multiplicity 1 (HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity); and for every x ∈ ∂*E and compact K, L^{n+1}(K ∩ (η_{x,r}(E) Δ {y : ⟨y, ν_E(x)⟩ > 0})) → 0 as r ↓ 0.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 3, (4.2) and Theorem 4.3 with its proof, chapter-03.txt lines 576-746 (printed pp. 81-83). Errata and gaps (stated explicitly): (E1) sign: in the display after (8) (lines 674-686) the printed “0 ≤ ρ_k^{-n}∫ζ_kν_{n+1}dμ_E = ∫_{ρ_k^{-1}E}D_{n+1}ζ” drops the minus sign of (8)/(4.1); correctly ∫_{ρ_k^{-1}E}D_{n+1}ζ = −ρ_k^{-n}∫ζ_kν_{n+1}dμ_E ≤ o(1), so χ_H is non-decreasing (as printed) and (9) and the final display must read {x^{n+1} > λ}, {x^{n+1} > 0} (printed “<”), consistent with (4.1) and (‡‡); (E2) “χ_{ρ_k^{-1}E} → χ_R” (line 655) should read χ_F; (E3) the last step (lines 739-746, “Then by 4.1, (1) and (2) we have μ_{ρ^{-1}E} → Hⁿ⌞{x^{n+1} = 0}”) is terse: it also uses the mass bound (6) to control ∫φ(1 − ν_{n+1})dμ_ρ; written out in Part 4; (E4) “By 1.6 and 3.6 of Ch. 1, the first part of the theorem follows from (‡)” (line 604) is only a sketch: Theorem 1.6 concerns Hⁿ⌞M, not μ_E, so we use the measure form of the 1.6 “⇐” argument (sibling rectifiable_of_tangent_measure) and density comparison (Part 5); (E5) “Repeating the same argument with U ∖ E in place of E” (line 729) uses that (μ, −ν) is a Gauss-Green pair for U ∖ E (Part 1); (E6) for n = 0 the Sobolev inequality is replaced by its one-dimensional L^∞ form.

Notation. N := n + 1; ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N); L^N = volume; Hⁿ = μHE[n]; B_ρ(x) open ball; ω_d = L^d(B_1(0)) (ω₀ = 1); η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x) (blowUpMap); e_N the last basis vector. A Gauss-Green pair (μ, ν) for (U, E) is as in IsGaussGreenPair: μ Borel, μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, ν μ-measurable, |ν| = 1 μ-a.e., and (GG) ∫_{E∩U} div g = −∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ for C¹ g with compact support in U. By mollification (g_σ → g uniformly, div g_σ → div g a.e. and boundedly, supports in a fixed compact subset of U), (GG) also holds for Lipschitz g with compact support in U. normalAverage(x, ρ) := μ(B_ρ(x))⁻¹∫_{B_ρ(x)} ν dμ (:= 0 if the denominator is 0 or ∞), ∂*E := {x ∈ U : normalAverage(x, ρ) converges as ρ ↓ 0 to a unit vector}, ν_E(x) := the limit (reducedNormal).

Statement. DeGiorgiTheorem: for U ⊆ ℝ^N open and E Lebesgue-null-measurable with HasLocallyFinitePerimeter U E: (0) a Gauss-Green pair exists; and for every Gauss-Green pair (μ, ν): (R) ∂*E is countably n-rectifiable; (M) μ = Hⁿ⌞∂*E; (‡) for every x ∈ ∂*E, HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x P_x 1 with P_x := (span{ν_E(x)})^⊥; (‡‡) for every x ∈ ∂*E and compact K, L^N(K ∩ (η_{x,r}(E) Δ {y : ⟨y, ν_E(x)⟩ > 0})) → 0 as r ↓ 0.

Part 0. (0) is the “⇒” direction of the sibling gauss_green (GaussGreenRepresentation). Fix a pair (μ, ν).

Part 1. Invariances.
1a (complement; erratum E5). (μ, −ν) is a Gauss-Green pair for (U, U ∖ E): ∫_{(U∖E)∩U} div g = ∫_U div g − ∫_{E∩U} div g = 0 + ∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ (∫_{ℝ^N} ∂ᵢgⁱ = 0 for compactly supported C¹ g by Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus). Its reduced boundary is ∂*E with normal −ν_E (normalAverage is linear in ν).
1b (scaling, translation, rotation). For x ∈ ℝ^N, r > 0 and an orthogonal R, put E' := R(η_{x,r}(E)), U' := R(η_{x,r}(U)), μ'(B) := r^{-n}μ(η_{x,r}⁻¹(R⁻¹B)) and ν'(y) := Rν(η_{x,r}⁻¹(R⁻¹y)). Then (μ', ν') is a Gauss-Green pair for (U', E') (change of variables y = R η_{x,r}(z): for g' ∈ C¹_c(U'), g := R⁻¹∘g'∘R∘η_{x,r} ∈ C¹_c(U) satisfies div g(z) = r⁻¹(div g')(Rη_{x,r}(z)) and ⟨g(z), ν(z)⟩ = ⟨g'(Rη_{x,r}(z)), Rν(z)⟩ and ∫_{E'∩U'} div g' = r^{-N}·r∫_{E∩U} div g = −r^{-n}∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ = −∫⟨g', ν'⟩dμ'), and normalAverage'(R η_{x,r}(z), ρ) = R normalAverage(z, rρ). Hence z ∈ ∂*E iff Rη_{x,r}(z) ∈ ∂*E' with ν_{E'} = Rν_E. All conclusions (‡), (‡‡) at a point x₀ ∈ ∂*E are equivalent to the corresponding conclusions at 0 for the pair obtained with x = x₀, r = 1 and R with Rν_E(x₀) = e_N. So, in Parts 2-4, 0 ∈ ∂*E and ν_E(0) = e_N.
1c. For x ∈ ∂*E, 0 < μ(B_ρ(x)) for every ρ > 0 (otherwise normalAverage(x, ρ') = 0 for ρ' ≤ ρ and the limit would be 0), and μ(B_ρ(x)) < ∞ for ρ < ρ₀(x) := dist(x, ℝ^N ∖ U) (B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ U compact); here dist(x, ∅) := +∞ (in Lean use infEdist, since Metric.infDist x ∅ = 0).

Part 2. Density estimates at 0 (Simon (1)-(6), lines 607-652). Let ρ₀ := ρ₀(0), V(ρ) := L^N(E ∩ B_ρ(0)), V_c(ρ) := L^N(B_ρ(0) ∖ E) (non-decreasing, hence differentiable a.e.).
(1) ⨍_{B_ρ} ν_N dμ := μ(B_ρ)⁻¹∫_{B_ρ}ν_N dμ → 1 (the N-th component of normalAverage(0, ρ) → (ν_E(0))_N = 1).
(2) ⨍_{B_ρ}|ν − e_N| dμ → 0, in particular ⨍_{B_ρ}|νᵢ| dμ → 0 for i < N: as |ν| = 1 a.e., |ν − e_N|² = 2(1 − ν_N), so ⨍|ν − e_N| ≤ (⨍|ν − e_N|²)^{1/2} = (2(1 − ⨍ν_N))^{1/2} → 0.
(3) For a Lipschitz ζ ≥ 0 with compact support in U, (GG) with g = ζe_N gives ∫ζν_N dμ = −∫_E D_Nζ ≤ ∫_E|Dζ|, and with 1a, ∫ζν_N dμ = ∫_{U∖E} D_Nζ ≤ ∫_{U∖E}|Dζ|.
(4)-(5) Let ρ ∈ (0, ρ₀) be a point where V and V_c are differentiable. For k with 1/k < ρ let ζ_k(y) := φ_k(|y|), φ_k := 1 on [0, ρ − 1/k], 0 on [ρ, ∞), linear in between. Then ζ_k ↑ 1_{B_ρ(0)} pointwise, |Dζ_k| = k on the annulus {ρ − 1/k < |y| < ρ} and 0 a.e. elsewhere, so ∫_E|Dζ_k| = k(V(ρ) − V(ρ − 1/k)) → V'(ρ) and similarly for V_c. By dominated convergence (|ν_N| ≤ 1, μ(B_ρ) < ∞), (3) gives
 (5) ∫_{B_ρ(0)} ν_N dμ ≤ min(V'(ρ), V_c'(ρ)) for a.e. ρ ∈ (0, ρ₀).
(6) By (1) choose ρ₁ ∈ (0, ρ₀) with ∫_{B_ρ}ν_N dμ ≥ μ(B_ρ)/2 for ρ < ρ₁. Since V(ρ) − V(ρ') ≤ L^N(B_ρ ∖ B_{ρ'}), V'(ρ) ≤ Nω_Nρⁿ. Hence μ(B_ρ(0)) ≤ 2V'(ρ), μ(B_ρ(0)) ≤ 2V_c'(ρ) and μ(B_ρ(0)) ≤ 2Nω_Nρⁿ for a.e. ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁); by monotonicity of ρ ↦ μ(B_ρ) (letting a.e. ρ' ↓ ρ) the last bound holds for every ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁): (6') μ(B_ρ(0)) ≤ Cρⁿ, C := 2Nω_N.

Part 3. Blow-ups of E are half-spaces (Simon lines 653-737, with E1, E2). For r > 0 let E_r := η_{0,r}(E), U_r := η_{0,r}(U) (⊇ B_{ρ₀/r}(0)), μ_r(B) := r^{-n}μ(rB), ν^{(r)}(y) := ν(ry); (μ_r, ν^{(r)}) is a Gauss-Green pair for (U_r, E_r) by 1b.
3a. Bounds: for R > 0 and r < ρ₁/R, μ_r(B_R(0)) = r^{-n}μ(B_{rR}(0)) ≤ CRⁿ, and for C¹ g with |g| ≤ 1 and compact support in B_R(0) ⊆ U_r, ∫_{E_r} div g = −∫⟨g, ν^{(r)}⟩dμ_r ≤ μ_r(B_R) ≤ CRⁿ. So the characteristic functions χ_{E_r} are bounded in L¹(B_R) and have uniformly bounded variation |Dχ_{E_r}|(B_R) ≤ CRⁿ (Simon Ch. 2 (2.4)).
3b. Compactness (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 2.6, chapter-02.txt lines 598-628, proved there by mollification and Arzelà's theorem with reference to [GT01, Thm 7.22]; we write out this route, since BV compactness is not available in SimonGMT/Mathlib). Claim: every sequence r_k ↓ 0 has a subsequence with χ_{E_{r_k}} → u in L¹_loc(ℝ^N); passing to an a.e. convergent subsequence, u ∈ {0, 1} a.e., so u = χ_F for a Lebesgue measurable F (erratum E2). (i) Translation estimate: for R > 0, |h| ≤ 1 and r < ρ₁/(R+1), ∫_{B_R}|χ_{E_r}(y + h) − χ_{E_r}(y)| dy ≤ |h|·μ_r(B_{R+1}) ≤ |h|C(R+1)ⁿ. Indeed, for ψ ∈ C¹_c(B_R) with |ψ| ≤ 1, ∫(χ_{E_r}(y + h) − χ_{E_r}(y))ψ(y) dy = ∫χ_{E_r}(ψ(· − h) − ψ) = −∫₀¹∫_{E_r} div(ψ(· − th)h) dy dt = ∫₀¹∫⟨ψ(y − th)h, ν^{(r)}(y)⟩dμ_r(y) dt ≤ |h|μ_r(B_{R+1}) by (GG) for the scaled pair (the fields ψ(· − th)h are supported in B_{R+1} ⊆ U_r); take the supremum over such ψ (L¹(B_R) norm by duality and density of C¹_c in the unit ball of L^∞). (ii) Hence, with a standard mollifier φ_σ (σ ≤ 1), ‖χ_{E_r} − φ_σ * χ_{E_r}‖_{L¹(B_R)} ≤ ∫φ_σ(h)‖χ_{E_r}(· − h) − χ_{E_r}‖_{L¹(B_R)} dh ≤ σC(R+1)ⁿ. (iii) The functions φ_σ * χ_{E_r} take values in [0, 1] and are Lipschitz with constant σ⁻¹‖Dφ‖_{L¹}, uniformly in r. By Arzelà-Ascoli on B̄_m(0) and a diagonal argument over m ∈ ℕ (σ = 1/m, R = m), some subsequence r_k has φ_{1/m} * χ_{E_{r_k}} converging uniformly on B̄_m(0) for every m. Then, for fixed R and σ = 1/m with m ≥ R, ‖χ_{E_{r_k}} − χ_{E_{r_l}}‖_{L¹(B_R)} ≤ 2σC(R+1)ⁿ + ω_NR^N sup_{B_R}|φ_σ * χ_{E_{r_k}} − φ_σ * χ_{E_{r_l}}|, so (χ_{E_{r_k}}) is Cauchy in L¹(B_R) for every R and converges in L¹_loc.
3c. Horizontal invariance (Simon (7)-(8)). For ζ ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^N), spt ζ ⊆ B_R(0), and i < N: ∫_{E_r} Dᵢζ = −∫ζνᵢ^{(r)}dμ_r and |∫ζνᵢ^{(r)}dμ_r| ≤ sup|ζ| r^{-n}∫_{B_{rR}}|νᵢ|dμ ≤ sup|ζ| CRⁿ ⨍_{B_{rR}}|νᵢ| dμ → 0 by (2), (6'). L¹_loc convergence gives ∫_F Dᵢζ = 0 for all ζ ∈ C¹_c, i < N. Hence χ_F(x', t) is a.e. independent of x' ∈ ℝⁿ: mollifying, u_σ := φ_σ * χ_F is smooth with Dᵢu_σ = 0 (i < N), so u_σ(x', t) = w_σ(t), and u_σ → χ_F in L¹_loc; therefore F = ℝⁿ × H (up to a null set) for a measurable H ⊆ ℝ (for n = 0 there is nothing to prove).
3d. Vertical monotonicity (corrected sign, erratum E1). For ζ ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^N), ζ ≥ 0, spt ζ ⊆ B_R: ∫_{E_r}D_Nζ = −∫ζν_N^{(r)}dμ_r = −∫ζ dμ_r + ∫ζ(1 − ν_N^{(r)})dμ_r ≤ sup ζ · r^{-n}∫_{B_{rR}}(1 − ν_N)dμ ≤ sup ζ · CRⁿ(1 − ⨍_{B_{rR}}ν_N dμ) → 0 by (1), (6') (note 1 − ν_N ≥ 0). So ∫_F D_Nζ ≤ 0. With ζ(x', t) = α(x')β(t), α, β ≥ 0, ∫α = 1: ∫_H β'(t)dt ≤ 0 for all β ∈ C¹_c(ℝ), β ≥ 0, i.e. the distributional derivative of χ_H is a non-negative measure, so χ_H agrees a.e. with a non-decreasing {0, 1}-valued function: H = (λ, ∞) up to a null set, λ ∈ [−∞, ∞], and F = {x : x_N > λ} (erratum: printed (9) has “<”).
3e. λ = 0 (Simon lines 689-733, with E5, E6). Sobolev step: for ζ Lipschitz, ζ ≥ 0, compact support in U, and G ∈ {E, U ∖ E} with the corresponding pair (μ, ±ν):
 (S) ‖ζχ_G‖_{L^{N/(N−1)}} ≤ c_N(∫ζ dμ + ∫_G |Dζ|) if N ≥ 2, and ess sup ζχ_G ≤ ½(∫ζ dμ + ∫_G|Dζ|) if N = 1.
 Proof: for w ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^N), ‖w‖_{N/(N−1)} ≤ c_N‖Dw‖_1 (Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev inequality, [GT01, Thm 7.10]; Mathlib eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv_of_eq; for N = 1, sup|w| ≤ ½∫|w'|, from w(x) = ∫_{−∞}^x w' = −∫_x^∞ w'); it extends to Lipschitz w with compact support by applying it to φ_τ * w and letting τ → 0 (‖D(φ_τ * w)‖₁ ≤ ‖Dw‖₁). Apply it to w_σ := ζ·(φ_σ * χ_G) for small σ: ∫|Dw_σ| ≤ ∫ζ|D(φ_σ * χ_G)| + ∫(φ_σ * χ_G)|Dζ|, and ∫ζ|D(φ_σ * χ_G)| = sup_{|g|≤ζ, g ∈ C¹_c} ∫g·D(φ_σ * χ_G) = sup −∫_G div(φ_σ * g) = sup ±∫⟨φ_σ * g, ν⟩dμ ≤ ∫(φ_σ * ζ)dμ → ∫ζ dμ (|φ_σ * g| ≤ φ_σ * ζ; the easy half of Simon Ch. 2, Lemma 2.5); letting σ ↓ 0 (φ_σ * χ_G → χ_G in L¹_loc and boundedly) gives (S).
 Apply (S) with ζ = ζ_k from (4), k → ∞: for a.e. ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁), with (6), V(ρ)^{(N−1)/N} ≤ c_N(μ(B_ρ) + V'(ρ)) ≤ 3c_N V'(ρ) if N ≥ 2, and 1 ≤ 3V'(ρ)/2 whenever V(ρ) > 0 if N = 1 (ess sup ζ_kχ_E = 1 for large k when V(ρ) > 0). Moreover V(ρ) > 0 for all ρ > 0: otherwise χ_E = 0 a.e. on B_ρ, so ∫ζν_N dμ = −∫_E D_Nζ = 0 for ζ supported in B_ρ, and with ζ_k ↑ 1_{B_{ρ'}} (ρ' < ρ) this gives ∫_{B_{ρ'}}ν_N dμ = 0, contradicting (1) and 1c. For the non-decreasing W := V^{1/N} we get W'(ρ) = V'(ρ)/(N V^{(N−1)/N}) ≥ 1/(3c_N N) (N ≥ 2; for N = 1, W = V and W' ≥ 2/3) at a.e. ρ < ρ₁; since a non-decreasing function satisfies W(ρ) − W(ε) ≥ ∫_ε^ρ W'(t)dt (Lebesgue), letting ε ↓ 0 gives (10) V(ρ) ≥ c'ρ^N for ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁), c' := (3c_N N)^{-N} (resp. 2/3 for N = 1). The same argument for U ∖ E (1a, the second inequality in (5) and (6)) gives (11) V_c(ρ) ≥ c'ρ^N.
 Consequently, for every R > 0 and r < ρ₁/R, L^N(E_r ∩ B_R) = r^{-N}V(rR) ≥ c'R^N and L^N(B_R ∖ E_r) ≥ c'R^N; passing to the L¹_loc limit, L^N(F ∩ B_R) ≥ c'R^N and L^N(B_R ∖ F) ≥ c'R^N for every R > 0. If λ > 0 (or +∞) then F ∩ B_R = ∅ for R < λ; if λ < 0 (or −∞) then B_R ∖ F = ∅ for R < |λ|; both are impossible, so λ = 0 and F = F₀ := {x : x_N > 0}.
3f. (‡‡) (Simon lines 734-739). Every sequence r_k ↓ 0 has a subsequence along which χ_{E_{r_k}} → χ_{F₀} in L¹_loc. Hence χ_{E_r} → χ_{F₀} in L¹_loc as r ↓ 0 (otherwise some compact K, ε > 0 and r_k ↓ 0 would have L^N(K ∩ (E_{r_k} Δ F₀)) ≥ ε for all k, contradicting the subsequence property). Undoing the normalization 1b (x₀ ∈ ∂*E, R with Rν_E(x₀) = e_N; R maps {y : ⟨y, ν_E(x₀)⟩ > 0} onto F₀ and preserves L^N): L^N(K ∩ (η_{x₀,r}(E) Δ {y : ⟨y, ν_E(x₀)⟩ > 0})) → 0 for every compact K. (Only E ∩ U matters: for r < ρ₀(x₀)/R, η_{x₀,r}(E) ∩ B_R = η_{x₀,r}(E ∩ U) ∩ B_R.)

Part 4. (‡) (Simon lines 739-746: “by 4.1, (1) and (2)”, together with (6); erratum E3). Let P := e_N^⊥ = ℝⁿ × {0}. Note that ∫ f dμ_r = r^{-n}∫ f(η_{0,r}(y)) dμ(y), the quantity in HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) and R > 1 with spt f ⊆ B_{R−1}(0). (i) For φ ∈ C¹_c(B_R(0)) and r < ρ₁/R, (GG) for the scaled pair (μ_r, ν^{(r)}) with g = φe_N gives ∫φν_N^{(r)}dμ_r = −∫_{E_r}D_Nφ → −∫_{F₀}D_Nφ = ∫_P φ dHⁿ as r ↓ 0, by 3f (L¹_loc convergence; D_Nφ is bounded with compact support) and Fubini with the fundamental theorem of calculus in x_N. (ii) Since 1 − ν_N ≥ 0 μ-a.e., |∫φ(1 − ν_N^{(r)})dμ_r| ≤ sup|φ|·r^{-n}∫_{B_{rR}}(1 − ν_N)dμ ≤ sup|φ|·CRⁿ(1 − ⨍_{B_{rR}}ν_N dμ) → 0 by (1) and (6'). With (i): ∫φ dμ_r → ∫_P φ dHⁿ. (iii) For the given f and ε > 0 choose φ ∈ C¹_c(B_R(0)) with sup|f − φ| ≤ ε (mollification). Then |∫f dμ_r − ∫φ dμ_r| ≤ εμ_r(B_R) ≤ εCRⁿ and |∫_P f dHⁿ − ∫_P φ dHⁿ| ≤ εω_nRⁿ, so limsup_{r↓0}|∫f dμ_r − ∫_P f dHⁿ| ≤ ε(C + ω_n)Rⁿ; let ε ↓ 0. Hence HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ 0 P 1 (finrank P = n), i.e., after undoing 1b, (‡) holds at every x ∈ ∂*E with P_x = (span{ν_E(x)})^⊥. (For n = 0, P = {0}, H⁰⌞P is the unit mass at 0 and ω₀ = 1; the argument is unchanged.)

Part 5. Rectifiability and μ = Hⁿ⌞∂*E (erratum E4).
5a. μ(ℝ^N ∖ ∂*E) = 0 (Simon line 584, “by virtue of Theorem 3.23 of Ch. 1”).
